dogs/dachshund.description: The Dachshund is a German hound with a long body and short legs, bred to hunt badgers. Smooth, long or wire coat; lively, brave and often stubborn.
dogs/dachshund.answer: The Dachshund, also called the Dackel or Teckel, is a German breed of short-legged, long-bodied hound bred to scent, chase and flush out badgers and other burrow-dwelling animals. It comes in standard, miniature and, in FCI countries, rabbit sizes, with smooth, long-haired or wire-haired coats. The breed is usually described as clever, lively and courageous, but also stubborn.

faq.q: What does the name Dachshund mean?
faq.a: Dachshund is German for 'badger dog', from Dachs (badger) and Hund (dog). In Germany the breed is usually called Dackel, and hunters often call it Teckel.

faq.q: How long do Dachshunds live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.2 years for the breed and about 14 years for the miniature. Other studies have reported somewhat different figures.

faq.q: Why do Dachshunds have back problems?
faq.a: Their very long spine and short rib cage make them prone to intervertebral disc disease. Obesity, jumping and rough handling can add strain on the back.

faq.q: Is the Dachshund recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Dachshund as breed number 148 and gives it its own group, Group 4. It also recognises the rabbit size, which clubs in the US and UK do not.

dogs/golden-retriever.description: The Golden Retriever is a British gundog of medium-large size, bred in Scotland, with a golden or cream double coat and a gentle, affectionate temperament.
dogs/golden-retriever.answer: The Golden Retriever is a British retriever of medium-large size, bred in the late 19th century by Sir Dudley Marjoribanks at his Scottish estate, Guisachan. Dogs stand about 56 to 61 cm and bitches 51 to 56 cm. The breed is known for its gentle, affectionate nature and is widely kept as a companion and guide dog.

faq.q: How big does a Golden Retriever get?
faq.a: Under the Kennel Club standard, dogs stand 56 to 61 cm and bitches 51 to 56 cm. Healthy adults typically weigh 25 to 34 kg.

faq.q: Are Golden Retrievers good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as gentle and generally very tolerant of children, which is why it is popular as a family dog. Individual temperament still varies.

faq.q: How long do Golden Retrievers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a median life expectancy of 13.2 years. The breed has a high rate of cancer, which is a leading cause of death.

faq.q: Do Golden Retrievers shed?
faq.a: They have a long double coat with a dense undercoat, and the long hair needs regular grooming. It is more maintenance than a Labrador's short coat.

dogs/german-shepherd.description: The German Shepherd, or Alsatian, is a medium to large German working dog with a dense double coat, known for its intelligence, obedience and protectiveness.
dogs/german-shepherd.answer: The German Shepherd, known in Britain for decades as the Alsatian, is a German working dog of medium to large size developed from 1899 by Max von Stephanitz from traditional herding dogs. Breed standards give a height of 60 to 65 cm for males and 55 to 60 cm for females. It is described as intelligent, obedient and protective, and is widely used in police, military and search work.

faq.q: Is a German Shepherd the same as an Alsatian?
faq.a: Yes. The UK Kennel Club renamed the breed Alsatian after the First World War, and it was registered again as the German Shepherd from 1977; the word Alsatian was dropped from the formal name in 2010.

faq.q: How big does a German Shepherd get?
faq.a: The breed standard gives a height at the withers of 60 to 65 cm for males and 55 to 60 cm for females. It is classed as a medium to large dog.

faq.q: How long do German Shepherds live?
faq.a: Overall lifespan is approximately 10 years. A 2024 UK study found a mean of 11.3 years, slightly lower than the average for crossbreeds.

faq.q: Are German Shepherds good guard dogs?
faq.a: They are commonly described as protective, curious and wary of strangers, traits valued in guard and police work. Sources stress good socialization to avoid overprotectiveness.

dogs/rottweiler.description: The Rottweiler is a powerful medium-to-large German dog of mastiff type, black with rich tan markings, bred to drive cattle and guard, and known as territorial.
dogs/rottweiler.answer: The Rottweiler is a mastiff-type breed from Germany, named after the old free city of Rottweil, where butchers used it to herd livestock and pull carts of meat to market. Under the FCI standard males stand 61 to 69 cm and females 56 to 63 cm. It is described as strong and confident, with marked watchdog and territorial instincts.

faq.q: How big does a Rottweiler get?
faq.a: The FCI standard gives 61 to 69 cm at the withers for males and 56 to 63 cm for females, with weight in proportion to height. It is classed as a medium-to-large or large breed.

faq.q: How long do Rottweilers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 10.6 years, below the average for purebred dogs. Cancer is the most commonly reported cause of death.

faq.q: Why is it called a Rottweiler?
faq.a: The breed is named after the old free city of Rottweil in Germany, where butchers used the dogs to drive cattle and pull carts of meat.

faq.q: Is the Rottweiler recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Rottweiler as breed number 147 in Group 2, and the German ADRK is regarded as the breed's home club.

dogs/labrador-retriever.description: The Labrador Retriever is a medium-large British gun dog from Newfoundland stock, with a short dense water-resistant coat and a friendly, energetic nature.
dogs/labrador-retriever.answer: The Labrador Retriever, or Lab, is a British gun dog developed in the 19th century from St. John's water dogs imported from Newfoundland, now part of Canada. It is a medium-large breed; the FCI gives about 56 to 57 cm for dogs and 54 to 56 cm for bitches. Labradors are commonly described as friendly, energetic and playful, and are widely used as guide and assistance dogs.

faq.q: How big does a Labrador Retriever get?
faq.a: The FCI standard gives 56 to 57 cm for dogs and 54 to 56 cm for bitches; the AKC allows somewhat taller dogs. The AKC ideal weight is 25 to 36 kg for dogs and 25 to 32 kg for bitches.

faq.q: What colors do Labradors come in?
faq.a: Labradors are registered in three colors: solid black, yellow (from creamy white to fox-red) and chocolate. Puppies of all three colors can appear in the same litter.

faq.q: Are Labradors good family dogs?
faq.a: They are commonly described as friendly, playful and eager to work, and are among the most popular companion dogs in several countries. They need regular physical and mental exercise.

faq.q: Where does the Labrador come from?
faq.a: The breed was developed in the United Kingdom from St. John's water dogs imported from Newfoundland, and it is named after the Labrador region of that colony.

dogs/chihuahua.description: The Chihuahua is a Mexican toy breed and the smallest recognized dog breed, with an apple-domed head, large erect ears and a short or long coat.
dogs/chihuahua.answer: The Chihuahua, or Chihuahueño, is a Mexican toy breed and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. The FCI standard calls for an ideal weight of 1.5 to 2.5 kg, and dogs outside 1 to 3 kg are disqualified from shows. It is kept mainly as a companion and comes in short-coated and long-coated varieties.

faq.q: How big does a Chihuahua get?
faq.a: The FCI standard calls for 1.5 to 2.5 kg, and height is generally 15 to 23 cm. Pet Chihuahuas often weigh more than the show standard.

faq.q: How long do Chihuahuas live?
faq.a: Studies vary: a 2024 UK study and a Japanese cemetery study both found about 11.8 years, while other studies reported lower figures.

faq.q: Are Chihuahuas good with children?
faq.a: The American Kennel Club does not recommend Chihuahuas for families with young children, and the breed may show above-average aggression like many small dogs.

faq.q: What is a molera on a Chihuahua?
faq.a: The molera is a soft spot on the top of the skull, similar to the fontanel in human babies. It can be hard to see but is easy to feel.

dogs/shiba-inu.description: The Shiba Inu is a small-to-medium Japanese hunting dog with a double coat in red, sesame or black and tan, known as alert, independent and strong-willed.
dogs/shiba-inu.answer: The Shiba Inu is a Japanese hunting dog and the smallest of the six original dog breeds native to Japan. Its name means 'brushwood dog', and it was bred to flush small game in mountainous country. It is a small-to-medium breed described as alert, affectionate and independent, but also stubborn.

faq.q: What does Shiba Inu mean?
faq.a: The name literally translates as 'brushwood dog', referring to its use flushing game from brush. Inu is Japanese for dog.

faq.q: How long do Shiba Inus live?
faq.a: The Shiba is one of the longer-lived breeds: a Japanese study found 15.5 years and a 2024 UK study 14.6 years.

faq.q: Do Shiba Inus shed?
faq.a: They have a double coat with a soft, plush undercoat beneath stiff guard hairs. Sources give little detail on shedding, but double-coated breeds generally need regular brushing.

faq.q: Is the Shiba Inu the Doge meme dog?
faq.a: Yes. The 2013 Doge meme featured Kabosu, a Shiba Inu, and the Dogecoin cryptocurrency logo shows her image.

dogs/border-collie.description: The Border Collie is a medium-sized British herding dog from the Anglo-Scottish border, with a double coat in many colors and a reputation for intelligence.
dogs/border-collie.answer: The Border Collie is a medium-sized British herding dog of collie type from the region of the Anglo-Scottish border, descended from traditional British sheepdogs. Males stand 48 to 56 cm and females 46 to 53 cm. It is kept mainly for herding or as a companion, and some claim it is the most intelligent breed of dog.

faq.q: Is the Border Collie the smartest dog breed?
faq.a: Some have claimed it is the most intelligent breed, and individual dogs such as Chaser and Rico have been studied for learning hundreds of words. Intelligence rankings depend on how they are measured.

faq.q: How big does a Border Collie get?
faq.a: Males stand 48 to 56 cm at the withers and females 46 to 53 cm. It is a medium-sized breed.

faq.q: How long do Border Collies live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.1 years, and a 2022 English study found 12.1 years.

faq.q: Do Border Collies shed?
faq.a: Yes. Their double coat is often thick and prone to shedding, whether smooth or rough.

dogs/shih-tzu.description: The Shih Tzu is a small, sturdy toy breed of Tibetan and Chinese heritage, with a long double coat, a short muzzle and a lion-like look prized by royalty.
dogs/shih-tzu.answer: The Shih Tzu is a toy breed of Tibetan origin, believed to descend from the Pekingese and Lhasa Apso, and long kept by the Chinese royal court. Its name comes from the Mandarin word for lion. It is a sturdy little dog standing no more than about 27 cm, with a long, flowing double coat.

faq.q: What does Shih Tzu mean?
faq.a: The name comes from the Mandarin word for lion, because the dog was bred to resemble the lion of traditional Asian art. In England in the 1930s it was nicknamed the chrysanthemum dog.

faq.q: How big does a Shih Tzu get?
faq.a: A Shih Tzu should stand no more than about 27 cm at the withers. It is a small but sturdy toy breed.

faq.q: How long do Shih Tzus live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.8 years, close to the average for purebred dogs. A Japanese study found 15 years.

faq.q: How often should a Shih Tzu be brushed?
faq.a: The long double coat tangles and mats easily, so it should be brushed at least every two or three days.

dogs/bernese-mountain-dog.description: The Bernese Mountain Dog is a large Swiss farm and draft dog from the canton of Bern, with a long black, white and rust coat and a calm, attentive nature.
dogs/bernese-mountain-dog.answer: The Bernese Mountain Dog, or Berner Sennenhund, is a large breed from the canton of Bern and the Swiss Alps, one of four Sennenhund breeds. It was a general farm dog that guarded property, drove cattle and pulled carts of milk and cheese. Dogs stand about 64 to 70 cm and bitches 58 to 66 cm, and the breed is described as calm but energetic and attentive.

faq.q: How long do Bernese Mountain Dogs live?
faq.a: Life expectancy is short: several European studies found about 8 years, and a 2024 UK study found 10.1 years. Cancer is a leading cause of death.

faq.q: How big does a Bernese Mountain Dog get?
faq.a: Dogs stand about 64 to 70 cm and bitches 58 to 66 cm. Weights are roughly 35 to 55 kg for males and 35 to 45 kg for females.

faq.q: Are Bernese Mountain Dogs good with children?
faq.a: They are popular family dogs and are described as calm and indisposed to biting; trained dogs often give children rides in carts. They can be wary of strangers.

faq.q: Is the Bernese Mountain Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 45 in Group 2.

dogs/samoyed.description: The Samoyed is a medium-sized Siberian spitz with a thick white double coat, bred by the Nenets to herd and pull sleds, and known for its friendly nature.
dogs/samoyed.answer: The Samoyed is a spitz-type herding dog from Siberia, named after the Samoyedic peoples and descended from the Nenets Herding Laika. It is a medium-sized dog with a thick, white double coat, used for herding, hunting, protection and pulling sleds. The breed is known for a friendly, agreeable disposition and its 'Sammie smile'.

faq.q: Do Samoyeds shed a lot?
faq.a: Yes. The undercoat sheds heavily once or twice a year and fine hair sheds year-round, so the breed needs frequent grooming despite being marketed as hypoallergenic.

faq.q: How long do Samoyeds live?
faq.a: Life expectancy is about 12 to 13 years; a 2024 UK study found 13.1 years.

faq.q: Are Samoyeds good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as friendly, playful and good companions for small children and other dogs. They can bark a lot and may dig when bored.

faq.q: How big does a Samoyed get?
faq.a: Under the AKC standard males stand 53 to 60 cm and weigh 20 to 29 kg, and females stand 48 to 53 cm and weigh 16 to 23 kg.

dogs/poodle.description: The Poodle is a water dog of German or French origin with a thick, curly coat, in sizes from toy to standard, known as active, intelligent and trainable.
dogs/poodle.answer: The Poodle, Pudel in German and Caniche in French, is a water dog bred to retrieve game from water. Most cynologists place its origin in Germany, while the FCI holds that it is French. It comes in Standard, Medium, Miniature and Toy sizes, from 24 to 62 cm under the FCI standard, and is described as active, intelligent and particularly able to learn from humans.

faq.q: Is the Poodle German or French?
faq.a: Most cynologists believe it originated in Germany, but the FCI and a minority of experts consider it French. The German name Pudel means roughly 'splasher'.

faq.q: What sizes do Poodles come in?
faq.a: There are Standard, Medium, Miniature and Toy Poodles, though the Medium is not recognized by every club. Under the FCI standard they range from 24 cm (Toy) to 62 cm (Standard).

faq.q: Are Poodles hypoallergenic?
faq.a: They are often described that way because the curly coat traps hair and dander, but research has generally not found a difference in allergen levels between breeds.

faq.q: How long do Poodles live?
faq.a: Poodles tend to live 10 to 18 years, with smaller varieties living longer. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years.

dogs/american-pit-bull-terrier.description: The American Pit Bull Terrier is a medium-sized, short-haired, solidly built US breed of English bull-and-terrier descent, recognized by the UKC and ADBA.
dogs/american-pit-bull-terrier.answer: The American Pit Bull Terrier is a medium-sized, short-haired, solidly built dog developed in the United States from English bull-and-terrier ancestors. It is recognized by the United Kennel Club and the American Dog Breeders Association, but not by the American Kennel Club. Males are normally about 45 to 53 cm tall and females 43 to 50 cm, and the UKC describes the breed as strong, confident and eager to please.

faq.q: Is the American Pit Bull Terrier recognized by the AKC?
faq.a: No. It is recognized by the United Kennel Club and the American Dog Breeders Association, but not by the American Kennel Club or the FCI.

faq.q: How big does an American Pit Bull Terrier get?
faq.a: Males are normally about 45 to 53 cm and 15 to 27 kg, and females about 43 to 50 cm and 13 to 22 kg.

faq.q: Is a pit bull the same as an American Staffordshire Terrier?
faq.a: They share ancestry, and the UKC registers AmStaffs as American Pit Bull Terriers. Since 2015 the ADBA treats them as separate breeds, and breeders have pursued different goals for decades.

faq.q: How long do American Pit Bull Terriers live?
faq.a: The breed is described as hardy, with an average lifespan of at least 12 years, which is longer than many dogs of similar size.

dogs/beagle.description: The Beagle is a small-to-medium British scent hound bred to hunt hare and rabbit, with a smooth tricolor coat and a merry, even-tempered disposition.
dogs/beagle.answer: The Beagle is a British scent hound that looks like a small foxhound and was bred mainly to hunt rabbit and hare. The modern breed was developed in Great Britain around the 1830s and generally stands 33 to 40 cm at the withers. It is described as merry, gentle and even-tempered, and is widely kept as a companion and used as a detection dog.

faq.q: How big does a Beagle get?
faq.a: Beagles generally stand 33 to 40 cm at the withers, with females slightly smaller on average. The AKC splits them into 13-inch and 15-inch varieties.

faq.q: Are Beagles good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as excellent with children and get along well with other dogs and cats, which is why they are popular family pets.

faq.q: How long do Beagles live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years, close to the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Do Beagles bark a lot?
faq.a: Most bark when faced with something unfamiliar, and some bay when they catch a scent. Not all Beagles howl.

dogs/belgian-shepherd.description: The Belgian Shepherd is a medium-sized Belgian herding dog in four coat varieties, including the Malinois and Groenendael, described as intelligent and alert.
dogs/belgian-shepherd.answer: The Belgian Shepherd, or Chien de Berger Belge, is a medium-sized herding breed from Belgium bred in four varieties: the long-haired black Groenendael, rough-haired fawn Laekenois, short-haired fawn Malinois and long-haired fawn Tervueren. Dogs typically stand 56 to 66 cm and weigh 20 to 30 kg. The breed is described as highly intelligent, alert and hard-working, and is widely used by police and armed forces.

faq.q: Is the Malinois a separate breed from the Belgian Shepherd?
faq.a: The FCI and most kennel clubs treat the Malinois as one of four varieties of the Belgian Shepherd. The American Kennel Club recognizes it and the other three varieties as separate breeds.

faq.q: How big does a Belgian Shepherd get?
faq.a: Dogs typically stand 56 to 66 cm and weigh 20 to 30 kg, with bitches about 4 cm shorter on average. The ideal heights are 62 cm for dogs and 58 cm for bitches.

faq.q: How long do Belgian Shepherds live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found 12 years for the Malinois and 13.8 years for the Tervueren.

faq.q: Are Belgian Shepherds good family dogs?
faq.a: Many are kept as companions and adapt well to indoor life, but they need a lot of exercise and training. Some varieties are reported to be occasionally snappy with children.

dogs/jack-russell-terrier.description: The Jack Russell Terrier is a small British terrier, mainly white with smooth, rough or broken coat, bred for fox hunting and known as energetic and bold.
dogs/jack-russell-terrier.answer: The Jack Russell Terrier is a small British terrier descended from fox-working dogs bred in North Devon in the early 19th century by the Reverend John 'Jack' Russell. It is mostly white with dark or tan markings and a smooth, rough or broken coat. Under the FCI standard it stands about 25 to 30 cm, and it is described as intelligent, athletic, fearless and very energetic.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Jack Russell and a Parson Russell Terrier?
faq.a: They share an origin, but the Parson Russell is a show breed with a narrower height range, a longer head and a larger chest. The Jack Russell standard is broader and more work-based.

faq.q: How big does a Jack Russell Terrier get?
faq.a: The FCI standard calls for about 25 to 30 cm at the withers, while some working clubs allow 25 to 38 cm. It is a small terrier sized to follow foxes underground.

faq.q: How long do Jack Russell Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Are Jack Russells good with other pets?
faq.a: They have strong hunting instincts and may be aggressive toward other animals if not well socialized. Early socialization and training are commonly advised.

dogs/dobermann.description: The Dobermann, or Doberman Pinscher, is a medium-large German working dog of pinscher type, short-coated, and described as intelligent, alert and loyal.
dogs/dobermann.answer: The Dobermann, called the Doberman Pinscher in the US and Canada, is a German working dog of pinscher type bred around 1890 in Thuringia by tax collector Louis Dobermann. Dogs stand about 68 to 72 cm and bitches 63 to 68 cm. It is described as intelligent, alert and tenaciously loyal, and is kept as a guard dog or companion.

faq.q: Is a Dobermann the same as a Doberman Pinscher?
faq.a: Yes. Doberman Pinscher is the name used in the US and Canada, while most other countries, including Germany and Britain, use Dobermann.

faq.q: How big does a Dobermann get?
faq.a: Dogs stand about 68 to 72 cm and weigh 40 to 45 kg, and bitches stand 63 to 68 cm and weigh 32 to 35 kg.

faq.q: How long do Dobermanns live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.2 years, below the average for purebred dogs. Heart disease is a common cause of death.

faq.q: Are Dobermanns aggressive?
faq.a: They are often stereotyped that way, but one 2008 study found them very low in aggression toward owners and not an aggressive breed overall, though relatively high toward strangers.

dogs/chow-chow.description: The Chow Chow is a sturdy spitz-type breed from northern China with a dense smooth or rough double coat, a lion-like ruff and a unique blue-black tongue.
dogs/chow-chow.answer: The Chow Chow is a spitz-type breed originally from northern China and is considered a basal breed predating the modern breeds of the 19th century. It is sturdy and square in profile, with a broad skull, small erect ears and a very dense double coat that forms a ruff around the neck. Its purple or blue-black tongue and lips are unique among dog breeds.

faq.q: Why does a Chow Chow have a blue tongue?
faq.a: The purple or blue-black tongue and lips are a distinctive breed trait, and the gene appears to be dominant, so many Chow mixes keep it. The Shar Pei also has a blue-black tongue.

faq.q: How long do Chow Chows live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years, slightly below the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Where does the Chow Chow come from?
faq.a: The breed originated in northern China, and research suggests it descends from indigenous dogs of central China about 8,300 years ago.

faq.q: Is the Chow Chow recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Chow Chow as breed number 205 in Group 5, and FCI countries allow a self-colored nose in cream dogs.

dogs/australian-cattle-dog.description: The Australian Cattle Dog is a medium-sized Australian herding breed with a short red- or blue-speckled coat, bred to drive cattle, energetic and intelligent.
dogs/australian-cattle-dog.answer: The Australian Cattle Dog, nicknamed the Red or Blue Heeler, is a medium-sized herding breed developed in Australia to drove cattle over long distances and rough terrain. Females stand about 43 to 48 cm and males 46 to 51 cm. It is described as energetic, intelligent and independent, strongly attached to its owner and reserved with strangers.

faq.q: Is a Blue Heeler the same as an Australian Cattle Dog?
faq.a: Yes. Blue Heeler and Red Heeler are nicknames for the Australian Cattle Dog based on its coat color and its habit of nipping cattle at the heels.

faq.q: How long do Australian Cattle Dogs live?
faq.a: A small 2024 UK study found an average of 14 years, and many dogs remain active at 12 to 14 years of age.

faq.q: Are Australian Cattle Dogs good with children?
faq.a: They are described as good with older, considerate children but may nip at the heels of young children who run and squeal. Early socialization and supervision are advised.

faq.q: Do Australian Cattle Dogs shed?
faq.a: They are not year-round shedders but blow their coat about once a year, or twice in intact females. Otherwise they need little grooming.

dogs/kangal-shepherd-dog.description: The Kangal Shepherd Dog is a large Turkish livestock guardian from Sivas Province with a short fawn to wolf-grey coat and black mask, bred to guard flocks.
dogs/kangal-shepherd-dog.answer: The Kangal Shepherd Dog, or Turkish Kangal, is a traditional large livestock guardian from the Kangal district of Sivas Province in central Turkey. Dogs usually stand 72 to 78 cm and bitches 65 to 73 cm. Its coat ranges from pale fawn to wolf grey, always with a black mask, and it has long been kept with flocks to fend off wolves and other predators.

faq.q: How big does a Kangal get?
faq.a: Dogs usually stand 72 to 78 cm and weigh 48 to 60 kg, and bitches stand 65 to 73 cm and weigh 40 to 50 kg. It is a large breed.

faq.q: Is the Kangal the same as the Anatolian Shepherd?
faq.a: Not exactly. The Anatolian Shepherd is an American-developed type descended from Turkish guardian dogs, mainly Kangals, and Turkish authorities do not recognize it as a purebred Turkish breed.

faq.q: What is the Kangal used for?
faq.a: It is a traditional flock guardian that protects sheep from wolves and other predators. In Namibia and Kenya, Kangals protect livestock from cheetahs as part of a conservation program.

faq.q: Is the Kangal recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted the breed in 1989, and its most recent standard was published in 2018.

dogs/great-dane.description: The Great Dane, or Deutsche Dogge, is a giant short-haired German breed of mastiff-sighthound type, once a boar hunter and now mostly a companion dog.
dogs/great-dane.answer: The Great Dane is a giant German breed of mastiff-sighthound type, descended from medieval hunting dogs used on bear, boar and deer and kept as guard dogs by German nobility. Along with the Irish Wolfhound it is among the tallest breeds; the AKC sets a minimum of 76 cm for males and 71 cm for females. It is described as strong and elegant, and generally not unduly aggressive toward people or other animals.

faq.q: How big does a Great Dane get?
faq.a: The AKC standard requires males to be at least 76 cm and females at least 71 cm at the shoulder. A Great Dane named Zeus, at 111.8 cm, was the tallest dog on record.

faq.q: Is the Great Dane from Denmark?
faq.a: No. It is a German breed known in Germany as the Deutsche Dogge; the English name comes from the French Grand Danois, and the breed has no known link to Denmark.

faq.q: How long do Great Danes live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found an average life expectancy of 10.6 years, well below the average for purebred dogs. Heart disease and bloat are major causes of death.

faq.q: Are Great Danes aggressive?
faq.a: They are described as generally not unduly aggressive toward people and other animals. Individual temperament varies.

dogs/french-bulldog.description: The French Bulldog is a small companion breed from France with bat ears, a flat face and a short, fine coat, kept mainly as a family pet.
dogs/french-bulldog.answer: The French Bulldog is a small French companion breed that appeared in Paris in the mid-nineteenth century, apparently from Toy Bulldogs imported from England crossed with local ratters. It is muscular and compact, with a square head, bat-like ears and a flat face, and is now among the most frequently registered breeds in several countries.

faq.q: How big does a French Bulldog get?
faq.a: French Bulldogs typically stand about 23–36 cm and weigh about 7.5–15 kg; the AKC standard sets a maximum of 13 kg.

faq.q: How long do French Bulldogs live?
faq.a: Figures vary by source: a commonly cited figure is about 11 years, while a 2024 UK study found 9.8 years and a Japanese study 10.2 years.

faq.q: Why do French Bulldogs have breathing problems?
faq.a: Their shortened snout, known as brachycephaly, deforms the upper airway and can obstruct breathing and make it hard to cool down.

faq.q: Is the French Bulldog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the French Bulldog as breed number 101 in Group 9, companion and toy dogs.

dogs/pug.description: The Pug is a small companion breed from China with a wrinkled flat face, curled tail and short glossy coat, described as sociable and gentle.
dogs/pug.answer: The Pug is a small companion dog of Chinese origin, brought to Europe in the sixteenth century and popularized by the House of Orange and later Queen Victoria. It has a compact, square, muscular body, a wrinkled short-muzzled face and a curled tail, and is widely described as sociable and gentle.

faq.q: How big does a Pug get?
faq.a: Pugs are small dogs, commonly listed at about 30 cm tall and 6.3–8.1 kg.

faq.q: How long do Pugs live?
faq.a: A commonly cited figure is about 14 years, but studies vary: one UK study found 11.6 years and a Japanese study 12.8 years.

faq.q: Are Pugs good family dogs?
faq.a: Pugs were bred purely as companions and are commonly described as sociable, playful and gentle, thriving on human company.

faq.q: Is the Pug recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Pug as breed number 253 in Group 9, companion and toy dogs.

dogs/siberian-husky.description: The Siberian Husky is a medium-sized sled dog from the Russian Far East with a thick double coat, erect ears and a friendly, energetic nature.
dogs/siberian-husky.answer: The Siberian Husky is a medium-sized working sled dog of the Spitz family, developed by the Chukchi people of the Russian Far East. It has a dense double coat, erect triangular ears and varied markings, and is described as friendly, gentle and highly energetic.

faq.q: How big does a Siberian Husky get?
faq.a: Siberian Huskies typically stand about 51–60 cm and weigh about 16–28 kg, with females smaller than males.

faq.q: Are Siberian Huskies good with children?
faq.a: The ASPCA classifies the breed as good with children, though it notes high energy and special exercise needs.

faq.q: Do Siberian Huskies shed?
faq.a: Yes. The thick double coat sheds its undercoat and needs weekly grooming.

faq.q: How long do Siberian Huskies live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.9 years for the breed.

dogs/akita.description: The Akita is a large working breed from the mountains of northern Japan with a thick double coat and curled tail, known as loyal and reserved.
dogs/akita.answer: The Akita is a large Japanese working dog of spitz type from the mountains of northern Japan, with a separate American type developed after World War II. It is heavy-boned, with a thick double coat, erect ears and a tail curled over the back, and is generally described as territorial and reserved with strangers.

faq.q: How big does an Akita get?
faq.a: Akitas typically stand about 58–70 cm at the shoulder; large American-type males can weigh 45–59 kg.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Akita and the American Akita?
faq.a: American Akitas are generally larger and heavier-boned with a bear-like head and may be any color, while Japanese Akitas are lighter, more fox-like and limited to a few colors.

faq.q: How long do Akitas live?
faq.a: A commonly cited range is 10–12 years, and one UK study found a life expectancy of 11.4 years.

dogs/bull-terrier.description: The Bull Terrier is a medium-sized terrier from England with an egg-shaped head, triangular eyes and a short coat, described as even-tempered.
dogs/bull-terrier.answer: The Bull Terrier is an English terrier breed, developed in the mid-nineteenth century by James Hinks from bull-and-terrier dogs crossed with the English White Terrier. It is muscular and full-bodied, with a distinctive egg-shaped head and small triangular eyes, and is described as even-tempered and sociable. A separate Miniature Bull Terrier also exists.

faq.q: How big does a Bull Terrier get?
faq.a: Bull Terriers are commonly listed at about 53–56 cm at the shoulder, with a full, muscular body.

faq.q: Why do Bull Terriers have egg-shaped heads?
faq.a: Breeders selected away from a skull stop over many generations; Lord Gladiator in 1917 was the first dog with no stop at all.

faq.q: How long do Bull Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years, while an earlier UK survey gave a median of 10 years.

faq.q: Is the Bull Terrier recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Bull Terrier as breed number 11 in Group 3, terriers.

dogs/australian-shepherd.description: The Australian Shepherd is a medium-sized herding breed developed in the United States, with a wavy double coat and an intelligent, active nature.
dogs/australian-shepherd.answer: The Australian Shepherd, or Aussie, is a medium-sized herding dog developed in California in the nineteenth century, despite its name. It has a moderately long double coat in merle, black or red, and is described as intelligent, active and loyal.

faq.q: Are Australian Shepherds actually from Australia?
faq.a: No. The breed was developed in California; its name is linked to collies imported with sheep from Australia and New Zealand.

faq.q: How big does an Australian Shepherd get?
faq.a: Aussies typically stand 46–58 cm at the withers and weigh about 16–32 kg.

faq.q: How long do Australian Shepherds live?
faq.a: A commonly cited range is 13–15 years, and a 2024 UK study found a median of 13.7 years.

faq.q: Is the Australian Shepherd recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 342 in Group 1, sheepdogs and cattle dogs.

dogs/xoloitzcuintle.description: The Xoloitzcuintle, or Mexican hairless dog, is an ancient breed from Mexico in three sizes, hairless or coated, with a calm, attentive nature.
dogs/xoloitzcuintle.answer: The Xoloitzcuintle, or Xolo, is a hairless dog breed from Mexico whose name comes from the Aztec god Xolotl and the Nahuatl word for dog. It comes in standard, miniature and toy sizes and in hairless and coated varieties, and is described as calm and attentive.

faq.q: How big does a Xoloitzcuintle get?
faq.a: It depends on the size variety: Xolos range from about 23 to 67 cm and roughly 5 to 23 kg across toy, miniature and standard sizes.

faq.q: Are all Xolos hairless?
faq.a: No. Both hairless and coated puppies are usually born in the same litter; the coated form has a short, flat, dense coat.

faq.q: Is the Xoloitzcuintle recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 234 in Group 5, spitz and primitive types.

dogs/cavalier-king-charles-spaniel.description: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel is a small British toy spaniel with a silky feathered coat in four colours, described as playful and gentle.
dogs/cavalier-king-charles-spaniel.answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel is a British toy spaniel, recreated in the 1920s to resemble the spaniels of King Charles II's era. It is small for a spaniel, with a silky, feathered coat in four colours, and is described as playful, patient and eager to please.

faq.q: How big does a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel get?
faq.a: Cavaliers are small, typically about 30–33 cm tall and about 5.4–8 kg.

faq.q: How long do Cavalier King Charles Spaniels live?
faq.a: The lifespan is usually between eight and twelve years; a 2024 UK study found 11.8 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Cavalier and a King Charles Spaniel?
faq.a: The Cavalier is larger, with a flat skull, higher-set ears and a longer muzzle, while the King Charles Spaniel is smaller with a domed skull.

faq.q: Is the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 136 in Group 9, companion and toy dogs.

dogs/rhodesian-ridgeback.description: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large hound from southern Africa with a short wheaten coat and a reversed ridge of hair, described as dignified.
dogs/rhodesian-ridgeback.answer: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed from southern Africa, standardized in Bulawayo in what is now Zimbabwe in 1922. It is muscular, with a short light-to-red wheaten coat and a distinctive ridge of hair growing in the opposite direction along its back, and is described as dignified and intelligent.

faq.q: How big does a Rhodesian Ridgeback get?
faq.a: Ridgebacks typically stand about 61–69 cm at the withers and weigh roughly 32–37 kg.

faq.q: Do all Rhodesian Ridgebacks have a ridge?
faq.a: No. The ridge comes from a dominant mutation, and some purebred puppies are born without one; ridgelessness is the only disqualification in the AKC standard.

faq.q: How long do Rhodesian Ridgebacks live?
faq.a: A UK study found an average life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: Is the Rhodesian Ridgeback recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 146 in Group 6, scent hounds and related breeds.

dogs/alaskan-malamute.description: The Alaskan Malamute is a large spitz-type sled dog from Alaska, bred for strength and endurance, with a thick double coat and erect ears.
dogs/alaskan-malamute.answer: The Alaskan Malamute is a large spitz-type dog originally bred to haul heavy freight by sled, thought to have been developed by the Malimiut Inupiaq people of Alaska's Norton Sound region. It is heavier and more powerfully built than the Siberian Husky, with a dense double coat, erect ears and a plumed tail carried over the back.

faq.q: How big does an Alaskan Malamute get?
faq.a: Malamutes typically stand about 59–64 cm and weigh about 34–38 kg, though some individuals weigh 45 kg or more.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Malamute and a Siberian Husky?
faq.a: The Malamute is larger and heavier, bred for hauling heavy freight, while the Siberian Husky is smaller and bred for speed.

faq.q: How long do Alaskan Malamutes live?
faq.a: A commonly cited range is 10–12 years, and a 2024 UK study found an average of 11.3 years.

dogs/bulldog.description: The Bulldog is a medium-sized British breed of mastiff type with a large head, flat face and short coat, described as friendly and courageous.
dogs/bulldog.answer: The Bulldog, also called the English or British Bulldog, is a British breed of mastiff type developed as a companion from the extinct Old English Bulldog. It is stocky and muscular, with a large head, thick facial folds and a flat face with a protruding lower jaw, and is generally described as friendly and amiable.

faq.q: How big does a Bulldog get?
faq.a: Bulldogs are medium-sized; standards give about 25 kg for males and 23 kg for females, with lower weights in the United States.

faq.q: Are Bulldogs good with children?
faq.a: Bulldogs are known for getting along well with children, other dogs and other pets.

faq.q: How long do Bulldogs live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 9.8 years, and a 2022 UK study found 7.39 years.

faq.q: Is the Bulldog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Bulldog as breed number 149 in Group 2.

dogs/staffordshire-bull-terrier.description: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier is a small to medium terrier from England with a short, close coat and broad head, described as bold and family-friendly.
dogs/staffordshire-bull-terrier.answer: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier, or Staffy, is a small to medium terrier that originated in Staffordshire and the northern parts of Birmingham in England. It descends from nineteenth-century bull and terrier crosses, is muscular and broad-headed with a short coat, and is described by the Kennel Club as bold, fearless and well suited to families.

faq.q: How big does a Staffordshire Bull Terrier get?
faq.a: Staffords usually stand 36–41 cm at the withers and weigh about 11–17 kg, with bitches a little lighter than dogs.

faq.q: Are Staffordshire Bull Terriers good with children?
faq.a: The Kennel Club recommends the breed for families, and its standard notes a particular affinity with children.

faq.q: Is a Staffordshire Bull Terrier a pit bull?
faq.a: No. It is a separate recognised breed, though it shares bull and terrier ancestry with pit bull types and is often confused with them.

faq.q: How long do Staffordshire Bull Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years, and a 2022 UK study found 11.33 years.

dogs/vizsla.description: The Vizsla is a medium-sized Hungarian pointing dog with a short golden-rust coat and no undercoat, described as gentle, affectionate and lively.
dogs/vizsla.answer: The Vizsla, or Hungarian Pointer, is a medium-sized hunting dog from Hungary used to track, point and retrieve game on land and in water. It is lean and muscular with a short, golden-rust coat, and is described as lively, gentle-mannered and affectionate, yet fearless with a protective instinct.

faq.q: How big does a Vizsla get?
faq.a: Vizslas typically stand about 52–69 cm and weigh 18–30 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: Do Vizslas shed?
faq.a: Yes. Although the coat is short and has no undercoat, Vizslas shed in all seasons and benefit from regular brushing.

faq.q: How long do Vizslas live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.5 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Vizsla recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as the Hungarian Short-haired Pointer, breed number 57 in Group 7, pointing dogs.

dogs/borzoi.description: The Borzoi is a large Russian sighthound with a long snout and a silky, often wavy coat, formerly used for wolf hunting and described as calm.
dogs/borzoi.answer: The Borzoi, or Russian Hunting Sighthound, is a large Russian sighthound formerly used to hunt wolves and known as the Russian Wolfhound until 1936. It has a uniquely long snout and a silky, flat or wavy coat, and is described as affectionate, athletic and calm.

faq.q: How big does a Borzoi get?
faq.a: Borzois are large dogs, commonly listed at about 68–85 cm at the shoulder and around 45 kg.

faq.q: Is the Borzoi the same as the Russian Wolfhound?
faq.a: Yes. The breed was known as the Russian Wolfhound until 1936, reflecting its former use in wolf hunting.

faq.q: How long do Borzois live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found an average life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: Is the Borzoi recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as the Borzoi (Russian Hunting Sighthound), breed number 193 in Group 10, sighthounds.

dogs/maltese.description: The Maltese is a toy companion breed linked to Italy and Malta, weighing 3–4 kg, with a silky pure-white coat and a lively, affectionate nature.
dogs/maltese.answer: The Maltese is a toy companion breed with a long, silky, pure-white coat, hanging ears and a tail curved over its back, recognized by the FCI under the patronage of Italy. Its name recalls an ancient small white dog associated with the island of Malta, though the modern breed was shaped in the Victorian era. It weighs about 3–4 kg and is described as lively, calm and affectionate.

faq.q: How big does a Maltese get?
faq.a: Maltese are very small, typically about 20–25 cm tall and 3–4 kg in weight.

faq.q: Do Maltese shed?
faq.a: The Maltese is described as not shedding; its coat has no undercoat.

faq.q: How long do Maltese dogs live?
faq.a: A commonly cited figure is about 15 years; a 2024 UK study found 13.1 years and an Italian study 11 years.

faq.q: Is the Maltese recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Maltese as breed number 65 in Group 9, companion and toy dogs.

dogs/yorkshire-terrier.description: The Yorkshire Terrier is a British toy terrier from Yorkshire, weighing up to 3.2 kg, with a long silky blue-grey and tan coat and a playful nature.
dogs/yorkshire-terrier.answer: The Yorkshire Terrier, or Yorkie, is a British toy terrier that originated in nineteenth-century Yorkshire and is among the smallest of all dog breeds, weighing no more than 3.2 kg. Its long, fine, silky coat is dark steel-grey on the body and tan on the head, and it is described as playful and energetic.

faq.q: How big does a Yorkshire Terrier get?
faq.a: Yorkies are among the smallest dog breeds, with a standard weight of no more than 3.2 kg.

faq.q: Do Yorkshire Terriers shed?
faq.a: Yorkies shed less than many breeds, losing small amounts when bathed or brushed, but the long coat needs regular brushing.

faq.q: How long do Yorkshire Terriers live?
faq.a: The breed has an above-average life expectancy; UK studies have found about 12.5 to 13.3 years.

faq.q: Is the Yorkshire Terrier recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 86 in Group 3, terriers.

dogs/bichon-frise.description: The Bichon Frisé is a small Franco-Belgian toy dog of bichon type, about 5 kg, with a loosely curled pure-white coat and a soft thick undercoat.
dogs/bichon-frise.answer: The Bichon Frisé is a small Franco-Belgian toy dog of bichon type, whose name means curly-haired small dog. It stands about 23–30 cm and weighs around 5 kg, with a pure-white coat curled in loose spirals over a soft undercoat. It was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine in 1933 and the FCI in 1959.

faq.q: How big does a Bichon Frisé get?
faq.a: Bichons are small, standing about 23–30 cm at the withers and weighing around 5 kg.

faq.q: What colour is a Bichon Frisé?
faq.a: The coat is always pure white; only puppies under a year may show a slight beige tinge.

faq.q: How long do Bichon Frisés live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Bichon Frisé recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in October 1959.

dogs/dogo-argentino.description: The Dogo Argentino is a large mastiff-type dog from Córdoba, Argentina, with a short all-white coat, bred in the 1920s for hunting big game.
dogs/dogo-argentino.answer: The Dogo Argentino is a large Argentine dog of mastiff type, bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, central Argentina, mainly for hunting big game such as peccaries, wild boar and pumas. It is powerfully built, with a short coat that is always white.

faq.q: How big does a Dogo Argentino get?
faq.a: Dogos are large dogs, standing about 60–68 cm and weighing roughly 40–45 kg, with bitches slightly smaller.

faq.q: What was the Dogo Argentino bred for?
faq.a: It was bred in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting large game such as peccaries, wild boar and pumas.

faq.q: How long do Dogo Argentinos live?
faq.a: The dogs usually live for some 10 to 12 years.

faq.q: Is the Dogo Argentino recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 292 in Group 2.

dogs/irish-wolfhound.description: The Irish Wolfhound is a giant sighthound from Ireland with a hard, rough coat, among the largest dog breeds, known as gentle, loyal and reserved.
dogs/irish-wolfhound.answer: The Irish Wolfhound is a large sighthound from Ireland and one of the largest of all dog breeds, historically used for hunting wolves. It has a hard, rough coat and a long, muscular build, and is described as introverted, intelligent and reserved, with the motto gentle when stroked, fierce when provoked.

faq.q: How big does an Irish Wolfhound get?
faq.a: Irish Wolfhounds are among the largest breeds, typically about 71–79 cm or more at the shoulder and roughly 41–55 kg.

faq.q: How long do Irish Wolfhounds live?
faq.a: The breed has a relatively short lifespan; a 2024 UK study found 9.9 years, and older estimates were lower.

faq.q: Are Irish Wolfhounds good guard dogs?
faq.a: They are considered unreliable watchdogs because they are often friendly to strangers, though their size can deter intruders.

faq.q: Is the Irish Wolfhound recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 160 in Group 10, sighthounds.

dogs/newfoundland.description: The Newfoundland is a giant working dog from Newfoundland, Canada, with webbed paws and a thick water-resistant double coat, known for water rescue.
dogs/newfoundland.answer: The Newfoundland is a giant working dog originally bred for fishermen in Newfoundland, now part of Canada. With its muscular build, thick double coat, webbed paws and swimming ability, it is known above all for water rescue and lifesaving.

faq.q: How big does a Newfoundland get?
faq.a: Newfoundlands are giant dogs, typically about 66–71 cm tall and 54–68 kg, with large males weighing more.

faq.q: Are Newfoundlands good swimmers?
faq.a: Yes. Their webbed paws, muscular build and water-resistant coat make them strong swimmers, and they are known for water rescue.

faq.q: How long do Newfoundlands live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Newfoundland recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 50 in Group 2.

dogs/pyrenean-mountain-dog.description: The Pyrenean Mountain Dog, or Great Pyrenees, is a large white livestock guardian from the Pyrenees with a long thick double coat and double dewclaws.
dogs/pyrenean-mountain-dog.answer: The Pyrenean Mountain Dog, called the Patou in France and the Great Pyrenees in the United States, is a large livestock guardian dog from the Pyrenees, the mountains between France and Spain. It is powerfully built, with a long, thick, mostly white double coat, and is still widely used to protect flocks from wolves and bears.

faq.q: How big does a Pyrenean Mountain Dog get?
faq.a: It is a large breed: dogs stand 70–80 cm and bitches 65–75 cm, with adults typically weighing 55–75 kg.

faq.q: Is the Great Pyrenees the same as the Pyrenean Mountain Dog?
faq.a: Yes. Great Pyrenees is the American name for the Pyrenean Mountain Dog, known in France as the Patou.

faq.q: How long do Pyrenean Mountain Dogs live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study reported a median lifespan of 10.9 years.

faq.q: Is the Pyrenean Mountain Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 137 in Group 2.

dogs/presa-canario.description: The Presa Canario is a large, muscular mastiff-type dog from Spain's Canary Islands, bred for guarding and herding cattle, with a broad, square head.
dogs/presa-canario.answer: The Presa Canario is a large Spanish dog of mastiff or catch-dog type from the Canary Islands, found mostly on Gran Canaria and Tenerife. It stands roughly 56–65 cm and weighs about 40–65 kg, and was traditionally kept as a guard dog and for herding sheep and cattle.

faq.q: How big does a Presa Canario get?
faq.a: It is a large dog, roughly 56–65 cm at the withers and about 40–65 kg, with females usually smaller than males.

faq.q: How long do Presa Canarios live?
faq.a: One UK study found a median longevity of 7.7 years, well below the median for dogs overall.

faq.q: Is the Presa Canario recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it provisionally in 2001 under the name Dogo Canario, definitively in 2011, and renamed it Presa Canario in 2018.

dogs/weimaraner.description: The Weimaraner is a medium to large German hunting dog from the Weimar area, known for its silver-grey coat, amber eyes, speed, stamina and keen nose.
dogs/weimaraner.answer: The Weimaraner is a German all-purpose gun dog named after the city of Weimar, recognised as a breed in 1891. It stands about 57–70 cm and weighs roughly 25–40 kg, and is valued for its speed, stamina, nose and courage in the field.

faq.q: How big does a Weimaraner get?
faq.a: Males stand about 59–70 cm and weigh 30–40 kg; females are around 57–65 cm and 25–35 kg.

faq.q: How long do Weimaraners live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a median lifespan of 12.8 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is a Weimaraner a good family pet?
faq.a: The German breed club describes it as a hunting dog rather than a companion dog and says it needs real hunting work to stay balanced.

dogs/tibetan-mastiff.description: The Tibetan Mastiff is a large guardian breed from the Tibetan Plateau with a thick double coat, an independent mind and a reserved manner with strangers.
dogs/tibetan-mastiff.answer: The Tibetan Mastiff is a large flock-guarding dog bred in the high Himalayas and on the Tibetan Plateau. It stands roughly 61–66 cm, carries a dense double coat, and is described as intelligent, strong-willed and aloof with strangers.

faq.q: How big does a Tibetan Mastiff get?
faq.a: It stands roughly 61–66 cm; the American Kennel Club gives weights of 40–70 kg for males and 30–55 kg for females.

faq.q: Do Tibetan Mastiffs shed?
faq.a: They shed somewhat all year, with one heavy molt in late winter or early spring and sometimes a lighter one in late summer or autumn.

faq.q: Is a Tibetan Mastiff good for first-time owners?
faq.a: Sources say it is not recommended for novice owners because it is strong-willed, powerful and protective, and needs consistent training.

dogs/basset-hound.description: The Basset Hound is a short-legged, heavy-boned scent hound of French descent with long ears, loose skin and a mild, friendly, devoted temperament.
dogs/basset-hound.answer: The Basset Hound is a short-legged scent hound descended from French basset types and developed further in Britain to hunt rabbit and hare on foot. It stands about 33–38 cm but is heavy for its height, and is described as friendly, mild and devoted.

faq.q: How big does a Basset Hound get?
faq.a: It stands about 33–38 cm at the withers but is heavily built, with weights varying by bloodline, commonly in the 20–35 kg range.

faq.q: How long do Basset Hounds live?
faq.a: Lifespan is usually given as about 10–12 years; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years.

faq.q: Are Basset Hounds good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as friendly and tolerant of children and other pets, with a mild, devoted nature.

dogs/welsh-corgi.description: The Welsh Corgi is a small, low-set herding dog from Wales, recognised as two breeds, Pembroke and Cardigan, with a fox-like head and a water-resistant coat.
dogs/welsh-corgi.answer: The Welsh Corgi is a small herding dog from Wales that drove cattle by nipping at their heels. It exists as two separate breeds, the Pembroke and the larger, long-tailed Cardigan, both standing roughly 25–32 cm at the withers.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Pembroke and a Cardigan Corgi?
faq.a: The Cardigan is larger and heavier-boned, with rounded ears, a long tail and more permitted colors; the Pembroke is smaller, with pointed ears and a short or bobbed tail.

faq.q: Do Corgis shed?
faq.a: Yes. Both breeds have shedding double coats, with heavier sheds on average twice a year.

faq.q: How long do Corgis live?
faq.a: A 2004 Kennel Club survey found a median age at death of about 12 years for both the Pembroke and the Cardigan.

dogs/dalmatian.description: The Dalmatian is a muscular, medium-large dog from Croatia's Dalmatia region, famous for its spotted white coat, endurance and past as a carriage dog.
dogs/dalmatian.answer: The Dalmatian is a spotted dog whose origins the FCI places in Croatia and the historical region of Dalmatia. A muscular dog of roughly 54–62 cm with great stamina, it was used for hunting, guarding and running beside horse-drawn carriages, including fire engines.

faq.q: Do Dalmatians shed a lot?
faq.a: Yes. The standard short coat sheds considerably year-round, and the stiff hairs cling to fabric; weekly grooming reduces but does not prevent shedding.

faq.q: Are Dalmatians often deaf?
faq.a: Deafness is a recognised problem in the breed. Studies in several countries have found roughly 16–26% of tested dogs deaf in one or both ears.

faq.q: How long do Dalmatians live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.2 years, slightly above the average for purebred dogs.

dogs/west-highland-white-terrier.description: The West Highland White Terrier is a small Scottish terrier with a harsh white double coat, prick ears and a confident, energetic and independent character.
dogs/west-highland-white-terrier.answer: The West Highland White Terrier, or Westie, is a Scottish terrier bred to hunt small rodents. It stands about 25–28 cm and weighs around 7–9 kg, and is described as intelligent, self-assured and energetic, with a high prey drive.

faq.q: How big does a Westie get?
faq.a: Westies typically stand 25–28 cm at the withers and weigh about 6.8–9.1 kg.

faq.q: Are Westies good with children?
faq.a: Many are friendly with children, but they rarely tolerate rough handling such as ear or fur pulling, so supervision and early training are advised.

faq.q: How long do West Highland White Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 British study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years, and a 2015 French study found 12.93 years.

dogs/greyhound.description: The Greyhound is a tall, smooth-coated sighthound developed in Britain from ancient stock, known for racing speed and a gentle, affectionate, quiet temperament.
dogs/greyhound.answer: The Greyhound is an ancient sighthound bred to hunt by sight and speed, later used for coursing and racing; modern pedigree stock was registered in the United Kingdom. It stands about 68–76 cm, is slim and muscular, and is commonly described as gentle, sensitive and affectionate.

faq.q: How fast can a Greyhound run?
faq.a: Racing Greyhounds can reach peak speeds of at least 69 km/h, with typical winning speeds of about 58–61 km/h.

faq.q: Are Greyhounds good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as gentle and affectionate and can do well with children who are taught to treat the dog politely and respectfully.

faq.q: Do Greyhounds need to stay on a leash?
faq.a: Rehoming groups recommend it outside fully fenced areas, because many Greyhounds have a strong prey drive and little recall.

dogs/american-staffordshire-terrier.description: The American Staffordshire Terrier is a medium-sized, short-coated, muscular dog from the US, described by the AKC as confident, smart and good-natured.
dogs/american-staffordshire-terrier.answer: The American Staffordshire Terrier, or AmStaff, is a medium-sized, short-coated American breed descended from British bull-and-terrier dogs. It stands about 43–48 cm and weighs roughly 18–32 kg, and the AKC describes it as confident, smart and good-natured.

faq.q: How big does an American Staffordshire Terrier get?
faq.a: It stands about 43–48 cm at the shoulder and weighs roughly 18–32 kg, with males usually larger.

faq.q: Is an AmStaff the same as a Pit Bull?
faq.a: They share ancestry, but decades of separate breeding for conformation have made the AmStaff a distinct breed, typically stockier than the American Pit Bull Terrier.

faq.q: How long do American Staffordshire Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years for the breed.

dogs/pekingese.description: The Pekingese is a small toy dog from China, once kept by the imperial court, with a flat face, large eyes, a heavy double coat and a compact, low body.
dogs/pekingese.answer: The Pekingese is a toy dog from China, favored as a companion by the Chinese imperial court and named after Peking (Beijing). It is compact and low, weighs around 5 kg, and is known for its flat face, large eyes, long double coat and rolling gait.

faq.q: How big does a Pekingese get?
faq.a: It is a toy breed standing about 15–23 cm and weighing around 5 kg; the AKC disqualifies dogs over 14 lb (6.4 kg).

faq.q: Do Pekingese shed?
faq.a: Yes. The double coat sheds heavily and needs frequent, thorough grooming to prevent mats.

faq.q: How long do Pekingese live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years for the breed.

dogs/cocker-spaniel.description: The Cocker Spaniel is a medium-small gun dog of British origin, bred to flush woodcock, now two breeds, English and American, with long ears and a silky coat.
dogs/cocker-spaniel.answer: Cocker Spaniel is the name for two related spaniel breeds, the English Cocker Spaniel and the smaller American Cocker Spaniel. Both descend from British gun dogs bred to flush and retrieve woodcock, and they stand roughly 34–41 cm depending on breed and sex.

faq.q: What is the difference between English and American Cocker Spaniels?
faq.a: The American Cocker is smaller, with a shorter back, domed head and shorter muzzle; the English Cocker is taller with a narrower head and chest.

faq.q: How big does a Cocker Spaniel get?
faq.a: American Cockers stand about 34–39 cm and weigh 11–14 kg; English Cockers stand about 38–41 cm and show dogs weigh 13–15 kg.

faq.q: Why is it called a Cocker Spaniel?
faq.a: The name comes from the dog's use in hunting woodcock.

dogs/miniature-schnauzer.description: The Miniature Schnauzer is a small German dog with a wiry double coat, bushy beard and eyebrows, described as alert, spirited, friendly and easy to train.
dogs/miniature-schnauzer.answer: The Miniature Schnauzer is a small German dog of Schnauzer type, developed in the late nineteenth century as a farm ratter. It stands 30–35 cm and weighs 4–8 kg, and the AKC standard describes it as alert, spirited, friendly and willing to please.

faq.q: How big does a Miniature Schnauzer get?
faq.a: The international standard gives a height of 30–35 cm and a weight of 4–8 kg, most often 4.5–7 kg.

faq.q: Are Miniature Schnauzers easy to train?
faq.a: They are usually described as easy to train, and Stanley Coren ranked them 12th of 140 breeds for working and obedience intelligence.

faq.q: How long do Miniature Schnauzers live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years, and a Japanese study found 13.4 years.

dogs/basenji.description: The Basenji is a small, short-coated hunting dog from Central Africa, known as the barkless dog for its yodel-like voice, erect ears and tightly curled tail.
dogs/basenji.answer: The Basenji is a small hunting dog bred from stock originating in Central Africa, including the Congo region. Standing about 40–43 cm and weighing 9.5–11 kg, it is famous for not barking in the usual way, instead making a yodel-like sound.

faq.q: Do Basenjis bark?
faq.a: Not in the usual way. Because of an unusually shaped larynx they make a yodel-like sound, which earns them the nickname barkless dog.

faq.q: How big does a Basenji get?
faq.a: Average height is about 40 cm for females and 43 cm for males, with weights of about 9.5 and 11 kg.

faq.q: How long do Basenjis live?
faq.a: A 2004 UK Kennel Club survey found a median lifespan of 13.6 years, with the oldest dog in the survey reaching 17.5.

dogs/havanese.description: The Havanese is a small bichon-type toy dog from Cuba with a long, soft, silky coat, a springy gait and a friendly, easily trained nature.
dogs/havanese.answer: The Havanese is a bichon-type toy dog and the national dog of Cuba, developed from the extinct Blanquito de la Habana. It stands about 22–29 cm, has a long, silky coat, and is known for its friendly, readily trained nature.

faq.q: How big does a Havanese get?
faq.a: It is a toy breed standing about 22–29 cm at the withers, with 23–27 cm considered ideal.

faq.q: How long do Havanese live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.5 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Are Havanese easy to train?
faq.a: They are described as friendly and readily trained, and are used as therapy, assistance and performing dogs.

dogs/bloodhound.description: The Bloodhound is a large, heavy-boned scent hound linked to Belgium's Saint-Hubert Abbey, famed for tracking people and described as gentle and affectionate.
dogs/bloodhound.answer: The Bloodhound is a large scent hound, known in French as the chien de Saint-Hubert, originally bred to hunt deer and boar and used since the Middle Ages to track people. It stands about 58–72 cm and weighs roughly 40–54 kg, and is reported to be gentle and tireless on a scent.

faq.q: How big does a Bloodhound get?
faq.a: It stands about 58–72 cm at the withers and typically weighs around 40–54 kg, with larger dogs preferred in the show ring.

faq.q: How long do Bloodhounds live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 9.3 years, shorter than the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Are Bloodhounds good family dogs?
faq.a: They are described as gentle, affectionate and even-tempered with people, though their tracking drive can make them willful and hard to train.

dogs/lhasa-apso.description: The Lhasa Apso is a small, long-lived dog from Tibet with a heavy, straight coat and a tail carried over the back, traditionally kept as an indoor watchdog.
dogs/lhasa-apso.answer: The Lhasa Apso is a small non-sporting breed from Tibet, traditionally kept as an interior watchdog at palaces and monasteries. Males stand about 25 cm, females slightly less, and the breed has a thick, heavy coat and a reputation for long life.

faq.q: How big does a Lhasa Apso get?
faq.a: Males stand about 25 cm at the withers, with females slightly smaller.

faq.q: How long do Lhasa Apsos live?
faq.a: It is considered a long-lived breed; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years.

faq.q: Is the Lhasa Apso recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted the breed in 1960.

dogs/whippet.description: The Whippet is a medium-sized British sighthound between the Greyhound and Italian Greyhound in size, with a short smooth coat and a gentle, calm temperament.
dogs/whippet.answer: The Whippet is a British sighthound that sits between the Greyhound and the Italian Greyhound in size, once called the poor man's racehorse. It stands about 44–51 cm, has a short, smooth coat, and is described as gentle, affectionate and calm at home but fast and lively outdoors.

faq.q: Do Whippets shed?
faq.a: Very little. Their short, smooth coat has no undercoat and is easy to care for.

faq.q: How fast can a Whippet run?
faq.a: Whippets can reach about 56 km/h and are considered the fastest dogs of their weight class.

faq.q: How long do Whippets live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years for the breed.

dogs/boston-terrier.description: The Boston Terrier is a small, compact dog from the US with a short muzzle, erect ears and tuxedo-like markings, described as friendly and easy to train.
dogs/boston-terrier.answer: The Boston Terrier is a small, compact breed that originated in Boston, Massachusetts, around 1870 and was accepted by the AKC in 1893. It weighs up to about 11 kg, has a short muzzle, erect ears and white tuxedo markings, and is described as eager to please and sociable.

faq.q: How big does a Boston Terrier get?
faq.a: International standards set a maximum weight of about 11 kg, and the AKC divides the breed into classes under 15 lb, 15 to under 20 lb, and 20 to 25 lb.

faq.q: Are Boston Terriers good with children?
faq.a: When properly socialized they are generally described as getting along well with children, older people and other pets.

faq.q: How long do Boston Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.8 years for the breed.

dogs/miniature-pinscher.description: The Miniature Pinscher is a small German dog of Pinscher type with a short, smooth coat, a compact build and a vigorous, alert and fearless presence.
dogs/miniature-pinscher.answer: The Miniature Pinscher, or Zwergpinscher, is a small German dog of Pinscher type, traditionally used to hunt mice and other vermin. It stands 25–30 cm and weighs 4–6 kg, and is described as vigorous, alert and self-possessed.

faq.q: How big does a Miniature Pinscher get?
faq.a: Both males and females stand 25–30 cm at the withers and weigh 4–6 kg.

faq.q: Do Miniature Pinschers shed?
faq.a: They have a short, smooth coat with no undercoat, which is generally considered easy to keep.

faq.q: Is a Miniature Pinscher a small Doberman?
faq.a: No. It is a German Pinscher-type breed; genetic research in 2017 found shared ancestry with the Toy Manchester Terrier.

dogs/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever.description: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized red gun dog from Canada, the smallest retriever, known as intelligent, energetic and eager to please.
dogs/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever.answer: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever, or toller, is a gun dog from Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, bred to lure waterfowl within range and then retrieve them. The smallest of the retrievers, it stands about 43–54 cm and weighs 17–23 kg, and is described as intelligent, alert and energetic.

faq.q: How big does a Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever get?
faq.a: It is the smallest retriever, standing roughly 43–54 cm and weighing about 17–23 kg, with females slightly smaller.

faq.q: What does tolling mean?
faq.a: Tolling is luring waterfowl within gunshot range; the dog romps at the water's edge, attracting curious ducks, then retrieves the shot birds.

faq.q: Are tollers good family dogs?
faq.a: They are described as affectionate and good with children, but they need a lot of daily exercise and mental stimulation.

dogs/shar-pei.description: The Shar Pei is a medium-sized guard dog from southern China, known for its deep wrinkles, harsh short coat, blue-black tongue and broad, padded muzzle.
dogs/shar-pei.answer: The Shar Pei is a medium-sized dog from southern China, traditionally kept as a property guardian and nearly extinct by the 1970s. It stands about 44–51 cm, has a short, very harsh coat, and is best known in the West for its deep wrinkles and blue-black tongue.

faq.q: How big does a Shar Pei get?
faq.a: Adults typically stand 44–51 cm at the withers and weigh about 16–20 kg.

faq.q: Why do Shar Peis have wrinkles?
faq.a: Heavy wrinkling was favored in Western breeding from the 1970s onward; a traditional, less wrinkled type is still kept in Hong Kong.

faq.q: How long do Shar Peis live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 10.6 years, below the average for purebred dogs.

dogs/afghan-hound.description: The Afghan Hound is a tall sighthound from the mountains of Afghanistan, known for its long, fine, silky coat and an aloof yet playful temperament.
dogs/afghan-hound.answer: The Afghan Hound is a sighthound from the cold mountains of Afghanistan, bred for speed and hunting game. It typically stands about 63 to 74 cm tall and weighs around 23 to 27 kg. It is often described as aloof and dignified, with a clownish side when playing.

faq.q: How big does an Afghan Hound get?
faq.a: Afghan Hounds typically stand about 63 to 74 cm at the shoulder and weigh roughly 23 to 27 kg.

faq.q: How long do Afghan Hounds live?
faq.a: A typical lifespan of about 12 to 14 years is often given, although one UK study found an average life expectancy of 11.1 years.

faq.q: Are Afghan Hounds easy to train?
faq.a: They have a reputation among trainers for slow obedience, and Stanley Coren's survey placed them last among the breeds ranked for obeying commands.

faq.q: Do Afghan Hounds need a lot of grooming?
faq.a: Yes. Their long, fine coat requires considerable care and grooming to stay in good condition.

dogs/shetland-sheepdog.description: The Shetland Sheepdog, or Sheltie, is a small herding dog from Scotland's Shetland Islands with a long double coat and a bright, willing temperament.
dogs/shetland-sheepdog.answer: The Shetland Sheepdog, often called the Sheltie, is a small herding breed from the Shetland Islands of Scotland. It stands about 33 to 40 cm tall and resembles a miniature Rough Collie. It is commonly described as clever, vocal, willing to please and trustworthy.

faq.q: Is a Shetland Sheepdog a mini Collie?
faq.a: It looks like a miniature Rough Collie, but it descends from small Spitz-type island sheepdogs crossed with collies rather than from shrunken Rough Collies.

faq.q: How long do Shelties live?
faq.a: One UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years, and a Japanese study found 14.3 years.

faq.q: Do Shelties shed?
faq.a: Shelties have a long double coat with a soft undercoat, so regular brushing is generally needed to manage loose hair.

faq.q: Are Shetland Sheepdogs smart?
faq.a: Stanley Coren ranked the breed 6th out of 138 for working intelligence, and Shelties do well in obedience and agility.

dogs/czechoslovakian-wolfdog.description: The Czechoslovakian Wolfdog is a wolfdog breed from Czechoslovakia, bred from Carpathian wolves and German Shepherds, with a thick silver-grey coat.
dogs/czechoslovakian-wolfdog.answer: The Czechoslovakian Wolfdog is a breed of wolfdog that began as a 1955 military experiment in Czechoslovakia crossing a Carpathian grey wolf with a German Shepherd. It is a large dog, with a breed standard minimum of 65 cm for males and 60 cm for females. Sources give little detail about its temperament.

faq.q: Is the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog part wolf?
faq.a: Yes. The breed was created by crossing Carpathian grey wolves with German Shepherds, followed by backcrossing to German Shepherds.

faq.q: Is the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1999 as breed number 332 in Group 1, Sheepdogs and Cattledogs.

faq.q: How big is a Czechoslovakian Wolfdog?
faq.a: The standard calls for a minimum height of 65 cm and weight of 26 kg for males, and 60 cm and 20 kg for females.

dogs/english-mastiff.description: The English Mastiff is a very large British dog breed with a massive head, short fawn, apricot or brindle coat, black mask and a gentle, docile nature.
dogs/english-mastiff.answer: The English Mastiff, often simply called the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large mastiff-type dog and the largest dog breed by mass. It typically stands about 70 to 76 cm tall and can weigh from roughly 54 to over 100 kg. Breed standards describe it as courageous yet docile, gentle and loyal.

faq.q: How big does an English Mastiff get?
faq.a: Mastiffs typically stand about 70 to 76 cm at the shoulder and weigh from around 54 to over 100 kg, making them the heaviest breed on average.

faq.q: How long do English Mastiffs live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 9 years for the breed.

faq.q: Are English Mastiffs good family dogs?
faq.a: Breed descriptions call them gentle, loyal and docile, but their great size means they need plenty of space.

faq.q: Is the English Mastiff recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as the Mastiff, breed number 264 in Group 2.

dogs/boxer.description: The Boxer is a medium to large German mastiff-type breed with a short fawn or brindle coat, a square muzzle and a bright, playful, protective temperament.
dogs/boxer.answer: The Boxer is a medium to large, short-haired mastiff-type breed developed in Germany in the late 19th century. It typically stands about 53 to 63 cm tall and weighs around 25 to 30 kg. The breed is commonly described as bright, energetic and playful, loyal to its family but wary of strangers.

faq.q: How long do Boxers live?
faq.a: Boxers typically live around 10 years; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.3 years and another survey a median of 10.25 years.

faq.q: Are Boxers good with children?
faq.a: Boxers are commonly described as patient, spirited and protective with children, which makes them a popular family breed.

faq.q: Why is it called a Boxer?
faq.a: The origin of the name is unclear. Popular stories link it to the dog's use of its paws, but several writers favor a derivation from German dialect words for the smaller Bullenbeisser.

faq.q: Is the Boxer recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Boxer as breed number 144 in Group 2, and it is in the Working Group of The Kennel Club and the AKC.

dogs/english-cocker-spaniel.description: The English Cocker Spaniel is a compact British gundog with long low-set ears, a silky coat in many colors and a friendly, cheerful, people-loving nature.
dogs/english-cocker-spaniel.answer: The English Cocker Spaniel is a British gun dog originally used to flush woodcock and other game toward the guns. It is a sturdy, compact dog standing about 38 to 41 cm tall and weighing around 13 to 15 kg. It is commonly described as active, good-natured and friendly, earning the nickname Merry Spaniel.

faq.q: What is the difference between an English and an American Cocker Spaniel?
faq.a: The American Cocker was developed from the English Cocker and is smaller, with a shorter snout. The two have been registered as separate breeds since the 1930s and 1940s.

faq.q: How long do English Cocker Spaniels live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years, and a 2024 Italian study found 13 years.

faq.q: Are English Cocker Spaniels good with children?
faq.a: With good early socialization they are said to get along well with people, children, other dogs and other pets.

faq.q: Is the English Cocker Spaniel recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 5 in Group 8.

dogs/italian-greyhound.description: The Italian Greyhound is a small, slender sighthound from Italy, under 5 kg, with a fine short coat, a high-stepping gait and a long history as a companion.
dogs/italian-greyhound.answer: The Italian Greyhound, or Piccolo Levriero Italiano, is the smallest of the sighthounds and comes from Italy. It stands 32 to 38 cm at the withers and weighs no more than about 5 kg. Bred to hunt hare and rabbit, it is now kept mostly as a companion dog.

faq.q: How big does an Italian Greyhound get?
faq.a: It stands 32 to 38 cm at the withers and weighs no more than about 5 kg, making it the smallest sighthound.

faq.q: How long do Italian Greyhounds live?
faq.a: Median longevity is reported at about 14 years, compared with about 12.5 years for dogs overall.

faq.q: How fast is an Italian Greyhound?
faq.a: It is capable of bursts of speed up to about 60 km/h (35 mph).

faq.q: Is the Italian Greyhound recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it in 1956 and lists it as the Italian Sighthound, number 200 in Group 10.

dogs/pembroke-welsh-corgi.description: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a small, short-legged cattle herding dog from Wales with erect ears, a fox-like head, a double coat and an alert, eager temperament.
dogs/pembroke-welsh-corgi.answer: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a cattle herding breed from Pembrokeshire, Wales, whose name means dwarf dog in Welsh. It is a small, low-set dog standing about 25 to 30 cm tall and weighing around 9 to 12 kg. It is commonly described as eager to please, alert and family-oriented, though it can be stubborn.

faq.q: Do Pembroke Welsh Corgis shed?
faq.a: Yes. Their double coat sheds heavily all year, with peaks in spring and autumn, though regular brushing keeps it manageable.

faq.q: How long do Pembroke Welsh Corgis live?
faq.a: They typically live about 9 to 15 years; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.2 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Pembroke and a Cardigan Corgi?
faq.a: The Pembroke is shorter in body, with smaller ears and slightly straighter legs, and the two were recognized as separate breeds in 1934.

faq.q: Are Pembroke Welsh Corgis good with children?
