faq.a: Most are described as behaving well around children and other pets, especially with early socialization, though young dogs may herd by nipping at ankles.

dogs/german-shorthaired-pointer.description: The German Shorthaired Pointer is a medium-sized German gun dog with a dense, short brown or black coat, bred to point, track and retrieve on land and in water.
dogs/german-shorthaired-pointer.answer: The German Shorthaired Pointer, or Deutsch Kurzhaar, is a continental pointing dog that originated in Germany in the 19th century. It is a medium-sized dog, with males standing about 62 to 66 cm and females a few centimeters less. It was bred as an all-purpose gun dog and may also be kept as a companion.

faq.q: How big does a German Shorthaired Pointer get?
faq.a: Males stand about 62 to 66 cm at the withers, and females about 3 or 4 cm less.

faq.q: How long do German Shorthaired Pointers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a median longevity of 13.4 years, slightly above the 12.5-year average for all dogs.

faq.q: What colors do German Shorthaired Pointers come in?
faq.a: They are brown or black, in solid, white with colored patches, or roan patterns.

faq.q: Is the German Shorthaired Pointer recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1954, and it is breed number 119 in Group 7.

dogs/english-springer-spaniel.description: The English Springer Spaniel is a medium-sized British gundog with a feathered liver or black and white coat, bred to flush and retrieve game.
dogs/english-springer-spaniel.answer: The English Springer Spaniel is a British gun dog traditionally used to flush, or spring, and retrieve game. It is a medium-sized, compact dog, and the UK breed standard calls for a height of about 51 cm. It is widely used as a sniffer dog, and its show and working lines look almost like different breeds.

faq.q: How big does an English Springer Spaniel get?
faq.a: The UK breed standard calls for about 51 cm at the withers. Show-line males usually weigh 18 to 27 kg, and working types can be lighter.

faq.q: How long do English Springer Spaniels live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.5 years, and a 2022 UK study found 11.92 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Springer and a Cocker Spaniel?
faq.a: The Springer is larger, with shorter, higher-set ears, a longer muzzle and a less abundant coat than the English Cocker.

faq.q: Do English Springer Spaniels shed?
faq.a: Yes. They normally shed in spring and summer and occasionally in autumn.

dogs/malinois.description: The Malinois is the short-haired fawn variety of the Belgian Shepherd, a medium-sized, athletic herding dog from Belgium known for intelligence and drive.
dogs/malinois.answer: The Malinois is the short-haired, fawn variety of the Belgian Shepherd, a medium-sized herding dog from Belgium. Belgian Shepherds typically stand 56 to 66 cm and weigh 20 to 30 kg. The breed is described as highly intelligent, alert and trainable, and the Malinois is especially active.

faq.q: Is a Malinois a separate breed from the Belgian Shepherd?
faq.a: Most kennel clubs, including the FCI, treat the Malinois as one of four varieties of the Belgian Shepherd, but the American Kennel Club recognizes it as a separate breed.

faq.q: How long do Belgian Malinois live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years for the Malinois.

faq.q: Why do police and the military use the Malinois?
faq.a: The breed is intelligent, highly trainable and vigilant, with a strong guarding instinct, which suits it to detection, patrol and security work.

faq.q: Is a Malinois a good family dog?
faq.a: Belgian Shepherds are protective of their families and adapt to indoor life, but the Malinois is very active and needs ample exercise and early training.

dogs/bullmastiff.description: The Bullmastiff is a large English guard dog bred from the Mastiff and Old English Bulldog, with a short fawn, red or brindle coat and black muzzle.
dogs/bullmastiff.answer: The Bullmastiff is a large English breed of mastiff type, developed in the 19th century by crossing the English Mastiff with the extinct Old English Bulldog. It typically stands about 61 to 69 cm tall and weighs roughly 41 to 59 kg. It was bred to help gamekeepers guard estates against poachers.

faq.q: How big does a Bullmastiff get?
faq.a: Bullmastiffs typically stand about 61 to 69 cm at the withers and weigh roughly 41 to 59 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: How long do Bullmastiffs live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 10.2 years for the breed.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Bullmastiff and a Mastiff?
faq.a: The Bullmastiff was created by crossing the Mastiff with the Old English Bulldog, and it is smaller than the English Mastiff.

faq.q: Is the Bullmastiff recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1955, and it is breed number 157 in Group 2.

dogs/airedale-terrier.description: The Airedale Terrier is the largest terrier breed, from Yorkshire, England, with a wiry black and tan coat and an intelligent, independent, loyal temperament.
dogs/airedale-terrier.answer: The Airedale Terrier is the largest of the terrier breeds and comes from the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire, England. It typically stands about 56 to 61 cm tall and weighs around 19 to 25 kg. It is commonly described as intelligent, independent, loyal and sometimes stubborn.

faq.q: Why is the Airedale called the King of Terriers?
faq.a: It is traditionally called the King of Terriers because it is the largest of the terrier breeds.

faq.q: Do Airedale Terriers shed?
faq.a: Airedales are described as not shedding much and instead need clipping or hand stripping every 6 to 8 weeks. Their coat is not proven to be hypoallergenic.

faq.q: How long do Airedale Terriers live?
faq.a: They typically live about 12 to 14 years; one UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: Are Airedales good with other pets?
faq.a: Like most terriers they have a strong instinct to chase small animals, so care is needed with small pets and livestock, especially if the dog is not well trained.

dogs/cairn-terrier.description: The Cairn Terrier is a small working terrier from the Scottish Highlands with a harsh, weather-resistant double coat in cream, wheaten, red, gray or brindle.
dogs/cairn-terrier.answer: The Cairn Terrier is a small terrier from the Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye, counted among Scotland's earliest working dogs. It stands roughly 28 to 31 cm tall and weighs about 6 to 7.5 kg. Its name comes from the stone cairns where it flushed out vermin.

faq.q: How big does a Cairn Terrier get?
faq.a: The ideal height is roughly 28 to 31 cm, with a weight of about 6 to 7.5 kg.

faq.q: How long do Cairn Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years, and a 2015 French study found 13.42 years.

faq.q: Why is it called a Cairn Terrier?
faq.a: The name comes from the cairns, or stone piles, where these terriers often flushed out vermin. It was adopted as a compromise name in 1909.

faq.q: Is the Cairn Terrier recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1963, and it is breed number 4 in Group 3.

dogs/giant-schnauzer.description: The Giant Schnauzer is a large German working dog with a dense, wiry, weatherproof coat and a distinct beard, bred to drive livestock and guard property.
dogs/giant-schnauzer.answer: The Giant Schnauzer, or Riesenschnauzer, is a German breed and the largest of the three Schnauzer breeds. It typically stands about 60 to 70 cm tall and weighs around 35 to 47 kg. Bred as a farm and guard dog, it is now widely used for police work and dog sports.

faq.q: How big does a Giant Schnauzer get?
faq.a: Giant Schnauzers typically stand about 60 to 70 cm at the withers and weigh roughly 35 to 47 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: How long do Giant Schnauzers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years for the breed.

faq.q: What colors do Giant Schnauzers come in?
faq.a: There are three color varieties: pepper and salt, pure black, and black and silver.

faq.q: Is the Giant Schnauzer recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 181 in Group 2.

dogs/scottish-terrier.description: The Scottish Terrier, or Scottie, is a small, short-legged terrier from Scotland with a hard wiry coat, erect ears and an independent, feisty temperament.
dogs/scottish-terrier.answer: The Scottish Terrier, popularly called the Scottie, is one of five terrier breeds from Scotland, originally bred to hunt vermin, badgers and foxes. It is small and sturdy, standing about 25 to 28 cm tall and weighing roughly 8.5 to 11 kg. It is described as independent, territorial and feisty, but very loyal to its family.

faq.q: How big does a Scottish Terrier get?
faq.a: Scotties typically stand about 25 to 28 cm at the withers and weigh roughly 8.5 to 11 kg.

faq.q: How long do Scottish Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.7 years for the breed.

faq.q: Are Scottish Terriers good with children?
faq.a: Properly socialized Scotties can suit a family and act as protectors, but they are not recommended for homes with small children or children inexperienced with dogs.

faq.q: What is Scottie cramp?
faq.a: Scottie cramp is an inherited, episodic disorder that affects the dog's ability to walk, usually when it is under stress. It is described as non-painful and not life-threatening.

dogs/irish-setter.description: The Irish Setter is a gundog from Ireland with a silky red or chestnut coat, bred to locate and point game birds, and known for a friendly, gentle temperament.
dogs/irish-setter.answer: The Irish Setter, or Red Setter, is a gundog from Ireland bred to locate and point upland game birds. It is a tall, deep-chested dog; the FCI standard calls for about 55 to 67 cm depending on sex. The breed is known for a friendly, gentle and affectionate temperament.

faq.q: How big does an Irish Setter get?
faq.a: The FCI standard calls for males of about 58 to 67 cm and females of about 55 to 62 cm, with males weighing roughly 29 to 34 kg.

faq.q: How long do Irish Setters live?
faq.a: Life expectancy tends to be around 11 to 12 years, and a 2024 UK study found 12.9 years.

faq.q: Are Irish Setters good family dogs?
faq.a: The breed is known for a friendly, gentle and affectionate temperament and is described as both a gundog and a family dog.

faq.q: Is the Irish Setter recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as the Irish Red Setter, breed number 120 in Group 7.

dogs/american-bulldog.description: The American Bulldog is a large, muscular mastiff-type dog from the United States with a short, smooth coat, descended from Old English farm bulldogs.
dogs/american-bulldog.answer: The American Bulldog is a large, muscular mastiff-type breed developed in the United States from the Old English Bulldog. Its ancestors worked on small farms and ranches as guardians, stock dogs and catch dogs. Most weigh between about 27 and 54 kg and stand 52 to 70 cm at the withers.

faq.q: How big does an American Bulldog get?
faq.a: Most weigh about 27 to 54 kg and stand 52 to 70 cm at the withers, though some non-standard dogs exceed this.

faq.q: How long do American Bulldogs live?
faq.a: A typical lifespan of about 10 to 15 years is commonly listed.

faq.q: Do American Bulldogs shed?
faq.a: They are light to moderate shedders with a short, smooth coat that needs little maintenance, but they tend to drool more than many breeds.

faq.q: Is the American Bulldog the same as the American Bully?
faq.a: No. The American Bully is a separate breed developed from the American Pit Bull Terrier and several bulldog breeds, recognized by the UKC in 2013.

dogs/coton-de-tulear.description: The Coton de Tulear is a small companion dog from Madagascar with a soft, fluffy, cotton-like white coat, a curled tail and a lively, merry expression.
dogs/coton-de-tulear.answer: The Coton de Tulear is a small Bichon-type companion dog named for the port of Tuléar (Toliara) in Madagascar, where it is the national dog. It stands about 22 to 30 cm tall and usually weighs around 3.5 to 6 kg. It is known for its cotton-like coat and is traditionally described as lively, bright and merry.

faq.q: Do Coton de Tulears shed?
faq.a: The Coton is described as a non-shedding, low-dander breed, though puppies may shed their puppy coat and the adult coat needs daily brushing.

faq.q: How long do Coton de Tulears live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study of 44 dogs found a life expectancy of 14.2 years.

faq.q: How big does a Coton de Tulear get?
faq.a: It typically stands about 22 to 30 cm tall and weighs around 3.5 to 6 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: Is the Coton de Tulear recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI published its breed standard in 1972, and it is breed number 283 in Group 9.

dogs/old-english-sheepdog.description: The Old English Sheepdog is a large English herding breed with a long, shaggy grey and white double coat covering its face, and a bear-like rolling gait.
dogs/old-english-sheepdog.answer: The Old English Sheepdog, often called the Bobtail, is a large herding breed that emerged in England from early pastoral dogs. It typically stands about 56 to 61 cm or more at the withers, with a compact body and a long, shaggy coat that covers the face and eyes. It is widely known as the Dulux dog from paint advertising.

faq.q: Do Old English Sheepdogs shed?
faq.a: The breed is described as shedding only when brushed, but the long, thick double coat needs substantial grooming.

faq.q: How long do Old English Sheepdogs live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years for the breed.

faq.q: Why is the Old English Sheepdog called a Bobtail?
faq.a: The nickname comes from the tradition of docking the breed's tail. Many countries now ban cosmetic docking, so tailed dogs are increasingly common.

faq.q: Is the Old English Sheepdog recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 16 in Group 1.

dogs/collie.description: The Collie is a type of medium-sized herding dog from Scotland and Northern England, lightly built with a pointed snout, agile, intelligent and gentle.
dogs/collie.answer: Collies are a distinctive type of herding dog that originated in Scotland and Northern England, covering many landraces and formal breeds such as the Rough, Smooth and Border Collie. They are medium-sized, fairly lightly built dogs with pointed snouts. Collies are known as active, agile and intelligent, with a strong herding instinct.

faq.q: Is the Collie a single breed?
faq.a: Collie describes a type of herding dog that includes many breeds and landraces. The American Kennel Club has a breed it calls the Collie, the name usually means the Rough Collie in parts of the US, and it often means the Border Collie in rural Britain.

faq.q: Are Collies good with children?
faq.a: Collie breeds are generally described as gentle, devoted and compatible with children, though individual personalities vary.

faq.q: Are Collies easy to train?
faq.a: Collies range from average to very biddable in trainability, and the Border Collie ranks first in Stanley Coren's intelligence list.

faq.q: What is MDR1 in Collies?
faq.a: MDR1 is a genetic mutation that makes affected dogs unusually sensitive to many drugs, including ivermectin. A simple test can identify a dog's status.

dogs/portuguese-water-dog.description: The Portuguese Water Dog is a medium-sized, robust water dog from Portugal's Algarve, with a curly or wavy low-shedding coat and an active, loyal nature.
dogs/portuguese-water-dog.answer: The Portuguese Water Dog is a medium-sized working water dog from the Algarve region of Portugal, where it herded fish into nets and carried messages between boats. It stands roughly 43 to 57 cm tall and weighs about 16 to 25 kg, and is generally described as intelligent, trainable and closely attached to its people.

faq.q: Do Portuguese Water Dogs shed?
faq.a: Their single-layered coat is described as non-shedding, though there is no scientific evidence that any dog breed is truly hypoallergenic. The coat needs frequent brushing and regular trimming.

faq.q: How big does a Portuguese Water Dog get?
faq.a: Typical height is about 43 to 57 cm at the withers and weight about 16 to 25 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: Is the Portuguese Water Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 37 in Group 8, with Portugal as the country of origin.

dogs/kooikerhondje.description: The Kooikerhondje is a small Dutch spaniel-type dog bred to lure ducks, with a wavy orange-red and white double coat and a white plumed tail.
dogs/kooikerhondje.answer: The Kooikerhondje is a small spaniel-type sporting dog from the Netherlands, developed around the 16th century to lure ducks into decoy traps. It stands roughly 35 to 42 cm tall and has a wavy orange-red and white coat with a plumed white tail.

faq.q: What was the Kooikerhondje bred for?
faq.a: It was bred to lure ducks into decoy traps by moving near the water, a technique modelled on the way foxes attract ducks.

faq.q: How big is a Kooikerhondje?
faq.a: It is a small dog, roughly 35 to 42 cm at the withers, with males slightly taller than females.

faq.q: Is the Kooikerhondje recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 314 in Group 8, with the Netherlands as the country of origin.

dogs/border-terrier.description: The Border Terrier is a small British terrier from the Anglo-Scottish border, with a harsh, weather-resistant double coat and a background in fox hunting.
dogs/border-terrier.answer: The Border Terrier is a small, rough-coated British terrier from the area of the Anglo-Scottish border, traditionally used to bolt foxes for the Border Hunt. It typically weighs about 5 to 7 kg and is built with long enough legs to follow horses and a body narrow enough to enter burrows.

faq.q: How long do Border Terriers live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.2 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: How big does a Border Terrier get?
faq.a: It is a small terrier, typically weighing about 5 to 7 kg, with males slightly larger than females.

faq.q: Is the Border Terrier recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 10 in Group 3, the terriers, with Great Britain as the country of origin.

dogs/tosa.description: The Tosa, or Japanese Mastiff, is a rare, very large dog from Japan's Shikoku island with a short, smooth red, brindle or fawn coat; some countries restrict it.
dogs/tosa.answer: The Tosa, also called the Japanese Mastiff, is a rare large breed that originated in Tosa on the island of Shikoku, Japan, in the second half of the 19th century. Size varies widely, with Japanese-bred dogs often weighing about 36 to 61 kg and dogs bred elsewhere frequently heavier.

faq.q: Is the Tosa banned in some countries?
faq.a: Yes. Ownership is banned or legally restricted in a number of countries, including the United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland, Denmark and New Zealand.

faq.q: How big does a Tosa get?
faq.a: Size varies a lot. Japanese-bred Tosas generally weigh about 36 to 61 kg, while dogs bred outside Japan are often considerably heavier.

faq.q: Is the Tosa recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 260 in Group 2, with Japan as the country of origin.

dogs/neapolitan-mastiff.description: The Neapolitan Mastiff is a massive Italian guard dog from Southern Italy, with loose, heavily wrinkled skin and a short coat, usually black, grey or leaden.
dogs/neapolitan-mastiff.answer: The Neapolitan Mastiff, or Mastino Napoletano, is a large, massive mastiff-type breed from Southern Italy, descended from the region's traditional guard dogs. It stands about 60 to 75 cm tall, weighs roughly 50 to 70 kg, and is known for its abundant loose skin.

faq.q: How long do Neapolitan Mastiffs live?
faq.a: They may be expected to live up to about 10 years, with a reported median lifespan of 9.3 years, lower than the median for dogs overall.

faq.q: How big does a Neapolitan Mastiff get?
faq.a: It typically stands about 60 to 75 cm at the withers and weighs about 50 to 70 kg.

faq.q: Is the Neapolitan Mastiff recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it in 1956 and lists it as breed number 197 in Group 2, with Italy as the country of origin.

dogs/korean-jindo.description: The Korean Jindo is a medium-sized, double-coated spitz-type dog from Jindo Island, South Korea, known for upright ears, a curled tail and strong loyalty.
dogs/korean-jindo.answer: The Korean Jindo is a medium-sized spitz-type dog native to Jindo Island in South Korea, where it is protected as a Natural Monument. It stands about 45 to 55 cm tall, weighs roughly 15 to 23 kg, and is best known for loyalty to its owner and a strong hunting drive.

faq.q: Are Jindo dogs loyal?
faq.a: Loyalty is the trait the breed is best known for. A famous Jindo named Baekgu returned to her original owner on Jindo Island after being sold to a family about 300 km away.

faq.q: How big does a Korean Jindo get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized dog, about 45 to 55 cm at the withers and roughly 15 to 23 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: Is the Korean Jindo recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI recognised it in 2005 and lists it as breed number 334 in Group 5, with South Korea as the country of origin.

dogs/japanese-spitz.description: The Japanese Spitz is a small companion spitz from Japan with a thick pure-white double coat, prick ears and a curled plumed tail; lively and loyal.
dogs/japanese-spitz.answer: The Japanese Spitz is a small to medium spitz-type companion dog developed in Japan in the 1920s and 1930s. It typically stands about 30 to 38 cm tall, has a thick pure-white double coat, and is commonly described as active, loyal and affectionate.

faq.q: Do Japanese Spitz shed?
faq.a: They have a thick double coat that needs regular brushing, about twice a week, though dirt does not stick to it and it is considered easy to groom.

faq.q: How long do Japanese Spitz live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13 years, slightly above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Are Japanese Spitz good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as affectionate, playful and particularly loving toward children, though any dog should be supervised around young children.

dogs/maremmano-abruzzese-sheepdog.description: The Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog is a large livestock guardian from central Italy, with a thick, rough solid-white coat and a calm, protective nature.
dogs/maremmano-abruzzese-sheepdog.answer: The Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog is a large Italian livestock guardian dog from central Italy, especially the Maremma and Abruzzo, used for centuries to protect sheep from wolves. It stands roughly 62 to 74 cm tall, weighs about 35 to 52 kg, and has a thick, rough white coat.

faq.q: What is the Maremma Sheepdog used for?
faq.a: It is a livestock guardian traditionally used to protect sheep from wolves, and it has also guarded cattle, and penguins from foxes in Australia.

faq.q: How big does a Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog get?
faq.a: It is a large dog, roughly 62 to 74 cm at the shoulder and about 35 to 52 kg, with some dogs considerably larger.

faq.q: Is the Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 201 in Group 1, with Italy as the country of origin.

dogs/flat-coated-retriever.description: The Flat-coated Retriever is a medium-large English gundog bred to retrieve on land and water, with a dense flat black or liver coat and a cheerful nature.
dogs/flat-coated-retriever.answer: The Flat-coated Retriever is an English gun dog developed in the mid-19th century to retrieve game on land and in water. It stands roughly 57 to 62 cm tall, weighs about 25 to 36 kg, and is often described as energetic, friendly and slow to grow up.

faq.q: How long do Flat-coated Retrievers live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.7 years, somewhat below the purebred average.

faq.q: What colours do Flat-coated Retrievers come in?
faq.a: Black is most common, followed by liver; yellow also occurs but is disqualified in conformation shows.

faq.q: Is the Flat-coated Retriever recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 121 in Group 8, with Great Britain as the country of origin.

dogs/king-charles-spaniel.description: The King Charles Spaniel, or English Toy Spaniel, is a small British toy breed with a domed head, short nose and long ears; quiet and affectionate.
dogs/king-charles-spaniel.answer: The King Charles Spaniel, also called the English Toy Spaniel, is a small toy spaniel from Great Britain, long associated with English royalty and King Charles II. It weighs about 3.6 to 6.3 kg and is commonly described as a quiet, friendly lapdog.

faq.q: What is the difference between a King Charles Spaniel and a Cavalier?
faq.a: The King Charles is smaller, about 3.6 to 6.3 kg, with a domed head and a flat face, while the Cavalier is larger with a flat skull, higher-set ears and a longer muzzle.

faq.q: How long do King Charles Spaniels live?
faq.a: The average lifespan is reported as about 10 to 12 years.

faq.q: Are King Charles Spaniels good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as bonding well with and tolerating children, but they do not accept rough handling.

dogs/bedlington-terrier.description: The Bedlington Terrier is a small English terrier from Northumberland with a lamb-like look, a linty non-shedding coat and a mild but plucky character.
dogs/bedlington-terrier.answer: The Bedlington Terrier is a small terrier named after the mining town of Bedlington in Northumberland, England, originally bred to hunt vermin. It stands about 41 cm tall, weighs roughly 8 to 10 kg, and is known for its lamb-like appearance and a temperament described as both gentle and tenacious.

faq.q: Do Bedlington Terriers shed?
faq.a: The coat is described as non-shedding with minimal odour, but it needs at least weekly grooming to remove dead hair.

faq.q: How long do Bedlington Terriers live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.7 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Why does a Bedlington Terrier look like a lamb?
faq.a: Its rounded head, topknot and soft, linty coat in blue, liver or sandy shades give it a lamb-like look, which led to the old nickname Rothbury's Lambs.

dogs/chinese-crested-dog.description: The Chinese Crested Dog is a small, fine-boned toy breed in hairless and powderpuff varieties, with large erect ears, little shedding and a playful air.
dogs/chinese-crested-dog.answer: The Chinese Crested Dog is a small, fine-boned toy breed that comes in two varieties, the hairless and the coated powderpuff, which can appear in the same litter. It stands about 23 to 33 cm tall and typically weighs 4.5 to 5.9 kg; despite its name, its origins are more likely in Mexico or Africa than in China.

faq.q: Do Chinese Crested Dogs shed?
faq.a: The breed is described as having little to no shedding. The powderpuff still needs regular brushing, and the hairless needs skin care.

faq.q: How long do Chinese Crested Dogs live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Is the Chinese Crested Dog really from China?
faq.a: Probably not. Because it shares its hairless mutation with the Xoloitzcuintli, its origins are thought to be in Mexico or Africa, although the FCI lists China as the country of origin.

dogs/american-cocker-spaniel.description: The American Cocker Spaniel is a small US sporting spaniel with a domed head, long ears and a silky feathered coat, known for its merry, even temper.
dogs/american-cocker-spaniel.answer: The American Cocker Spaniel is a small sporting spaniel from the United States that diverged from the English Cocker Spaniel during the 20th century. It stands about 34 to 39 cm tall, typically weighs around 11 to 14 kg, and is known as the Merry Cocker for its even, people-oriented temperament.

faq.q: How big does an American Cocker Spaniel get?
faq.a: It stands about 34 to 39 cm at the withers and usually weighs around 11 to 14 kg, with females slightly lighter.

faq.q: How long do American Cocker Spaniels live?
faq.a: Typical lifespan is about 10 to 14 years; one 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between American and English Cocker Spaniels?
faq.a: The American Cocker is smaller, with a rounder domed skull, rounder eyes and a shorter muzzle, while the English Cocker is slightly larger with a more setter-like head.

dogs/griffon-bruxellois.description: The Griffon Bruxellois, or Brussels Griffon, is a small, sturdy toy dog from Belgium with a short nose, domed head and rough or smooth coat; alert and devoted.
dogs/griffon-bruxellois.answer: The Griffon Bruxellois, or Brussels Griffon, is a toy dog from Brussels, Belgium, descended from small terrier-like stable dogs. It weighs about 3.5 to 6 kg, has a domed head, short nose and expressive face, and is described as alert, proud and very attached to its owner.

faq.q: How big does a Brussels Griffon get?
faq.a: It is a toy breed, standing about 23 to 28 cm and weighing roughly 3.5 to 6 kg.

faq.q: How long do Brussels Griffons live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years, slightly above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Are Brussels Griffons good with children?
faq.a: They are described as very good with children provided they are not teased, though they are not very patient and are sensitive to rough treatment.

dogs/pointer.description: The Pointer, or English Pointer, is a medium-sized, athletic British gundog with a short, fine coat, usually white with coloured patches, and an even nature.
dogs/pointer.answer: The Pointer, sometimes called the English Pointer, is a medium-sized pointing dog developed in England to find game birds and signal their position by standing still and pointing. Kennel Club standards call for about 61 to 69 cm in height, and the breed is described as adaptable, obedient and even-tempered.

faq.q: How long do Pointers live?
faq.a: The breed is considered generally healthy, with a life expectancy of about 13 to 14 years.

faq.q: Do Pointers retrieve game?
faq.a: A classically trained Pointer points and flushes game but does not usually retrieve it; specialist retrievers are often used for that.

faq.q: Is the Pointer recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the English Pointer as breed number 1 in Group 7, with Great Britain as the country of origin.

dogs/komondor.description: The Komondor is a large Hungarian livestock guardian with a long, corded white coat that looks like a mop, described as calm at home and fearless in defence.
dogs/komondor.answer: The Komondor, also called the Hungarian sheepdog, is a large livestock guardian from Hungary, famous for its long white corded coat that resembles a mop. Females are at least about 65 cm and males at least about 70 cm tall, weighing roughly 40 to 60 kg, and the breed is described as calm, independent and fiercely protective.

faq.q: Do Komondors shed?
faq.a: Once the cords have fully formed, moulting is minimal; the main shedding happens in puppyhood before the cords develop.

faq.q: How big does a Komondor get?
faq.a: It is a large breed: females are at least about 65 cm and males at least about 70 cm at the withers, weighing roughly 40 to 60 kg.

faq.q: Is the Komondor recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 53 in Group 1, with Hungary as the country of origin.

dogs/japanese-chin.description: The Japanese Chin is a small toy companion dog from Japan with a broad round head, large dark eyes and a silky single coat, described as charming and cat-like.
dogs/japanese-chin.answer: The Japanese Chin, also known as the Japanese Spaniel, is a toy lap and companion dog from Japan with a long aristocratic history. It stands about 25 cm at the withers and is known for its broad round head, short muzzle, silky single coat and cat-like manner.

faq.q: How long do Japanese Chins live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years.

faq.q: Are Japanese Chins good apartment dogs?
faq.a: They are described as moderately active dogs that enjoy walks but adapt well to small living spaces such as flats.

faq.q: Is the Japanese Chin recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 206 in Group 9, with Japan as the country of origin.

dogs/german-pinscher.description: The German Pinscher is a medium-sized, endangered German breed with a short, smooth black-and-tan or red coat, once kept as a stable dog and ratter.
dogs/german-pinscher.answer: The German Pinscher, or Deutscher Pinscher, is a medium-sized German breed in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group, essentially a short-haired counterpart of the Schnauzer. It stands about 45 to 50 cm tall, weighs 14 to 20 kg, and is now considered an endangered breed in Germany.

faq.q: How big does a German Pinscher get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized dog, about 45 to 50 cm at the withers and 14 to 20 kg, with dogs and bitches in the same range.

faq.q: Is the German Pinscher rare?
faq.a: Yes. It is listed as endangered in Germany; between 2008 and 2017 roughly 350 to 450 puppies were whelped each year.

faq.q: Is the German Pinscher recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it in 1955 and lists it as breed number 184 in Group 2, with Germany as the country of origin.

dogs/fox-terrier.description: The Fox Terrier is a small British terrier type in two breeds, Smooth and Wire, mostly white with tan or black markings, bred to drive foxes from their dens.
dogs/fox-terrier.answer: Fox Terrier is the name for two closely related British terrier breeds, the Smooth Fox Terrier and the Wire Fox Terrier, which differ mainly in coat. Both stand about 36 to 39 cm tall and weigh roughly 6.8 to 8.6 kg, and were originally bred to drive foxes out of their dens for hunting packs.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Smooth and a Wire Fox Terrier?
faq.a: They are essentially the same in build and size; the Smooth has a short, hard coat, while the Wire has a dense, crisp, wiry double coat.

faq.q: How long do Fox Terriers live?
faq.a: The average lifespan is around 15 years, and a Kennel Club survey reported a median age at death of 13 years and 2 months.

faq.q: How big does a Fox Terrier get?
faq.a: Both types typically stand about 36 to 39 cm at the withers and weigh about 6.8 to 8.6 kg.

dogs/fila-brasileiro.description: The Fila Brasileiro is a large Brazilian mastiff-type guard dog with thick, loose skin and a short dense coat; ownership is restricted in some countries.
dogs/fila-brasileiro.answer: The Fila Brasileiro is a large mastiff-type working dog from Brazil, used as a guard dog, for cattle herding and for big-game hunting. It stands about 60 to 75 cm tall, weighs at least 40 kg in bitches and more in males, and is known for its thick, loose skin and heavy build.

faq.q: Is the Fila Brasileiro banned in some countries?
faq.a: Yes. Ownership requires a court exemption in countries including the United Kingdom, Norway and Australia, and it is illegal to own and breed in Turkey.

faq.q: How big does a Fila Brasileiro get?
faq.a: Males stand about 65 to 75 cm and weigh at least 50 kg; bitches are slightly smaller at about 60 to 70 cm and at least 40 kg.

faq.q: Is the Fila Brasileiro recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 225 in Group 2, with Brazil as the country of origin.

dogs/american-eskimo-dog.description: The American Eskimo Dog is a white spitz companion dog of German Spitz descent, bred in the US in toy, miniature and standard sizes with a thick coat.
dogs/american-eskimo-dog.answer: The American Eskimo Dog is a spitz-type companion dog developed in the United States from German Spitz brought by European immigrants, and renamed during the era of World War I. It comes in toy, miniature and standard sizes, from about 22 to 50 cm tall, and typically lives around 12 to 14 years.

faq.q: How big does an American Eskimo Dog get?
faq.a: It depends on the variety: toys are about 22 to 30 cm, miniatures about 30 to 40 cm and standards about 38 to 50 cm at the withers.

faq.q: How long do American Eskimo Dogs live?
faq.a: Typical life expectancy is about 12 to 14 years.

faq.q: Is the American Eskimo Dog the same as a German Spitz?
faq.a: It descends from the German Spitz, but the two have diverged and their standards are now significantly different.

dogs/continental-toy-spaniel.description: The Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French toy spaniel, about 28 cm tall, with a mostly white coat and erect (Papillon) or drooping (Phalène) ears.
dogs/continental-toy-spaniel.answer: The Continental Toy Spaniel, or Épagneul Nain Continental, is a toy-sized spaniel from Belgium and France. It comes in two forms that differ only in the ears: the erect-eared Papillon and the drop-eared Phalène. It stands about 28 cm and weighs roughly 1.5 to 5 kg.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Papillon and a Phalène?
faq.a: Only the ears: the Papillon has erect ears and the Phalène has drooping ones. In all other respects they are identical and are treated as one breed by the AKC and the FCI.

faq.q: How big does a Continental Toy Spaniel get?
faq.a: It stands up to about 28 cm at the withers and weighs between 1.5 and 5 kg, split into two weight classes.

faq.q: How long do Papillons live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.5 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Continental Toy Spaniel recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 77 in Group 9, Companion and Toy Dogs.

dogs/brittany-spaniel.description: The Brittany Spaniel is a medium-sized French gun dog from Brittany, bred for bird hunting, with a short or absent tail and a pied, roan or tri-colour coat.
dogs/brittany-spaniel.answer: The Brittany Spaniel, or Épagneul Breton, is a French gun dog of spaniel type bred mainly for bird hunting. It developed in Brittany in north-west France between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries. It is a medium-sized, cobby dog standing about 45 to 53 cm, often with a naturally short tail.

faq.q: Is a Brittany a spaniel or a pointer?
faq.a: It is a spaniel-type gun dog, but it was bred to point game birds as well as retrieve them.

faq.q: How big does a Brittany Spaniel get?
faq.a: It typically stands about 45 to 53 cm at the withers. The American type is somewhat larger and weighs around 14 to 18 kg.

faq.q: How long do Brittany Spaniels live?
faq.a: Studies have found median longevity of 12.6 years in France and 11.1 years in the UK.

faq.q: Is the Brittany Spaniel recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 95 in Group 7, Pointing Dogs.

dogs/scottish-deerhound.description: The Scottish Deerhound is a very tall British sighthound, bred to course red deer, with a harsh grey coat and a build like a larger, heavier-boned Greyhound.
dogs/scottish-deerhound.answer: The Scottish Deerhound, or simply Deerhound, is a large sighthound from Scotland, once bred to hunt red deer by coursing. It looks like a bigger, heavier-boned Greyhound with a rough coat. It is one of the tallest sighthounds, standing about 71 to 76 cm or more.

faq.q: How big does a Scottish Deerhound get?
faq.a: Males are at least 30 inches tall and weigh about 39 to 50 kg; females are from 28 inches and about 34 to 43 kg.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Deerhound and a Greyhound?
faq.a: The Deerhound is larger and more heavily boned, with a rough coat. It is slower on smooth ground but can outrun a Greyhound on rough terrain.

faq.q: Is the Deerhound recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 164 in Group 10, Sighthounds.

dogs/affenpinscher.description: The Affenpinscher is a small German toy dog of Pinscher type, 25–30 cm tall, with a harsh, wiry coat, a monkey-like face and a past as a stable ratter.
dogs/affenpinscher.answer: The Affenpinscher is a small German toy dog of Pinscher type. It was once kept on farms and in stables to catch mice and rats and is now mostly a companion. It weighs about 4 to 6 kg, stands 25 to 30 cm, and is known for its rough coat and monkey-like expression.

faq.q: Why is it called an Affenpinscher?
faq.a: Affe is German for ape or monkey, a reference to the dog's monkey-like expression. Pinscher refers to its breed type.

faq.q: Is the Affenpinscher a terrier?
faq.a: No. Despite the nickname Monkey Terrier, it is classed with the Pinschers and Schnauzers.

faq.q: How big does an Affenpinscher get?
faq.a: It generally weighs 4 to 6 kg and stands about 25 to 30 cm at the withers.

faq.q: What colours do Affenpinschers come in?
faq.a: FCI and UK standards accept only black. The American Kennel Club also allows grey, silver, red, black and tan, and beige.

dogs/english-setter.description: The English Setter is a medium-sized British gun dog with a silky white coat flecked with colour, known as belton, and a gentle, people-oriented temperament.
dogs/english-setter.answer: The English Setter is a medium-sized gun dog from Britain, bred to find and point game birds such as quail, pheasant and grouse. Its mainly white coat is flecked with colour, a pattern called belton. The breed standard sums up its character as a Gentleman by Nature.

faq.q: Are English Setters good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as intensely friendly and particularly happy with children.

faq.q: What is a Llewellin Setter?
faq.a: A Llewellin Setter is an English Setter descended from the 19th-century strain of breeder Richard Purcell Llewellin, not a separate breed.

faq.q: Is the English Setter recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 2 in Group 7, Pointing Dogs.

dogs/karelian-bear-dog.description: The Karelian Bear Dog is a medium-sized Finnish hunting spitz with a black-and-white coat, bred to bay big game such as bears and moose; fearless and tenacious.
dogs/karelian-bear-dog.answer: The Karelian Bear Dog is a Finnish hunting breed seen by many in Finland as a national treasure. It was bred to find and bark at big game, including brown bears, moose and wild boar. It is a medium-sized, black-and-white spitz standing about 49 to 60 cm.

faq.q: Is the Karelian Bear Dog good with other pets?
faq.a: It is usually described as aggressive towards other animals, so socialization with other house animals is advised.

faq.q: How big does a Karelian Bear Dog get?
faq.a: Males stand 54 to 60 cm and weigh 25 to 28 kg; females are 49 to 55 cm and 17 to 20 kg.

faq.q: Is the Karelian Bear Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 48 in Group 5, Spitz and Primitive Types.

dogs/german-wirehaired-pointer.description: The German Wirehaired Pointer, or Deutsch Drahthaar, is a German pointing dog of Griffon type with a wiry coat, standing about 57–68 cm at the withers.
dogs/german-wirehaired-pointer.answer: The German Wirehaired Pointer, known in Germany as the Deutsch Drahthaar, is a German pointing dog of Griffon type. It is closely related to the other German pointers and stands about 57 to 68 cm at the withers. It is a widely kept hunting breed in its homeland.

faq.q: What is a Deutsch Drahthaar?
faq.a: Deutsch Drahthaar is the German name of the German Wirehaired Pointer, a wire-coated German pointing dog.

faq.q: How big is a German Wirehaired Pointer?
faq.a: It stands about 57 to 68 cm at the withers.

faq.q: How long do German Wirehaired Pointers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a median longevity of 13 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the German Wirehaired Pointer recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted in 1954 and is FCI breed number 98 in Group 7, Pointing Dogs.

dogs/kai-ken.description: The Kai Ken is a rare, medium-sized Japanese hunting dog from Yamanashi with a brindle coat, prick ears and a reputation as agile, alert and loyal to family.
dogs/kai-ken.answer: The Kai Ken, also called the Tora Inu or Tiger Dog, is a rare Japanese breed from the Kai region of Yamanashi Prefecture. It is one of six native Japanese breeds protected by the Nihon Ken Hozonkai. It is a medium-sized, brindle-coated hunting dog, typically described as agile, alert and loyal.

faq.q: Why is the Kai Ken called the Tiger Dog?
faq.a: Its brindle coat has tiger-like stripes, giving it the name Tora Inu, or Tiger Dog.

faq.q: Are Kai Ken good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as friendly and often good with children, though reserved with strangers.

faq.q: How big does a Kai Ken get?
faq.a: Males typically stand 18 to 22 inches at the shoulder and females 17 to 20 inches.

faq.q: Is the Kai Ken recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is listed as FCI breed number 317 in Group 5, Spitz and Primitive Types.

dogs/galgo-espanol.description: The Galgo Español, or Spanish Greyhound, is a lean Spanish sighthound bred to course hare, lighter than a Greyhound, with a smooth or rough coat.
dogs/galgo-espanol.answer: The Galgo Español, or Spanish Greyhound, is a Spanish sighthound bred specifically for coursing hare and other game. It resembles the Greyhound but is lighter, with flatter muscling suited to endurance. It stands about 58 to 72 cm and comes in smooth and rough coats.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Galgo and a Greyhound?
faq.a: The Galgo is lighter, higher in the rear and has flatter muscling, a longer tail and a less deep chest. It also comes in a rough coat as well as a smooth one.

faq.q: How big does a Galgo Español get?
faq.a: It stands about 58 to 72 cm at the withers.

faq.q: Is the Galgo Español recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 285 in Group 10, Sighthounds.

dogs/puli.description: The Puli is a small-to-medium Hungarian herding dog with a long, corded coat, usually black, described as intelligent, active, loyal and wary of strangers.
dogs/puli.answer: The Puli is a small-to-medium Hungarian herding dog known for its long, corded coat, whose tight curls resemble dreadlocks. It has herded sheep on the Hungarian plain for centuries. It stands about 36 to 45 cm and is commonly described as intelligent, energetic and devoted.

faq.q: Do Pulis shed?
faq.a: The breed has little to no shedding, but its corded coat needs considerable grooming.

faq.q: How big does a Puli get?
faq.a: It stands about 36 to 45 cm and weighs roughly 10 to 15 kg.

faq.q: Are Pulis good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as very friendly, especially towards children, though sensitive and wary of strangers.

faq.q: Is the Puli recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 55 in Group 1, Sheepdogs and Cattle Dogs.

dogs/standard-schnauzer.description: The Standard Schnauzer is a medium-sized German working dog with a hard, wiry salt-and-pepper or black coat and a bristly beard; once a farm ratter.
dogs/standard-schnauzer.answer: The Standard Schnauzer, or Mittelschnauzer, is a German breed in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group, developed in southern Germany from the 1880s. It is a robust, square, medium-sized dog of about 45 to 50 cm with a bristly beard and whiskers. It is one of three Schnauzer breeds, alongside the Giant and the Miniature.

faq.q: How big does a Standard Schnauzer get?
faq.a: It usually stands 45 to 50 cm at the withers and weighs about 14 to 20 kg.

faq.q: How long do Standard Schnauzers live?
faq.a: Median lifespan is reported to be 13 years.

faq.q: What colours do Standard Schnauzers come in?
faq.a: Salt-and-pepper or black. Salt-and-pepper dogs always have a darker mask.

faq.q: Is the Standard Schnauzer recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted in 1955 and is FCI breed number 182 in Group 2.

dogs/chesapeake-bay-retriever.description: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a large American retriever from Maryland with a wavy, oily, waterproof coat, bred for icy-water duck work; bright and loyal.
dogs/chesapeake-bay-retriever.answer: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a large American retriever developed around Maryland's Chesapeake Bay in the 19th century. It was used to retrieve waterfowl, pull fishing nets and rescue fishermen, and is now mainly a family pet and hunting companion. It stands about 53 to 66 cm and weighs 25 to 37 kg.

faq.q: How big does a Chesapeake Bay Retriever get?
faq.a: It stands about 53 to 66 cm at the withers and weighs about 25 to 37 kg.

faq.q: Are Chesapeake Bay Retrievers good family dogs?
faq.a: They are described as excellent family dogs when properly socialized, though some can be willful and reserved with strangers.

faq.q: Is the Chesapeake Bay Retriever recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 263 in Group 8.

dogs/spanish-water-dog.description: The Spanish Water Dog is a medium-sized, athletic Spanish water dog with a curly, woolly coat that can cord, once used for herding, retrieving and fishing work.
dogs/spanish-water-dog.answer: The Spanish Water Dog, or Perro de Agua Español, is a medium-sized water dog from Spain. It was traditionally used to herd sheep and cattle, retrieve game in marshlands and help inshore fishermen. Today it is kept mainly as a companion and is known for its curly coat.

faq.q: How big does a Spanish Water Dog get?
faq.a: Males stand 44 to 50 cm and weigh 18 to 22 kg; females are 40 to 45 cm and 14 to 18 kg.

faq.q: How long do Spanish Water Dogs live?
faq.a: Life expectancy is thought to be about 14 years.

faq.q: Does the Spanish Water Dog have a corded coat?
faq.a: Its curly, woolly coat may form cords when it is grown long.

faq.q: Is the Spanish Water Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted in 1999 and is FCI breed number 336 in Group 8.

dogs/tibetan-terrier.description: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized, square dog from Tibet with a long, shaggy double coat and broad snowshoe feet, described as affectionate and lively.
dogs/tibetan-terrier.answer: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized dog that originated in Tibet, where it is known as the Tsang Apso. Despite its English name it is not a terrier; European travellers named it for its resemblance to terrier breeds. It stands about 36 to 41 cm and has a long, shaggy coat.

faq.q: Is the Tibetan Terrier a real terrier?
faq.a: No. It was named by European travellers for its resemblance to terriers but is not a member of the terrier group.

faq.q: Do Tibetan Terriers shed?
faq.a: They do not shed like short-coated dogs, instead losing hair at a rate similar to humans, though puppies drop their coat at about nine months.

faq.q: How long do Tibetan Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.8 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Tibetan Terrier recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 209 in Group 9, Companion and Toy Dogs.

dogs/bouvier-des-flandres.description: The Bouvier des Flandres is a large, rough-coated herding dog from Flanders, Belgium, with a heavy beard, described as gentle, loyal and protective.
dogs/bouvier-des-flandres.answer: The Bouvier des Flandres is a herding dog from Flanders, Belgium, whose name means cow herder of Flanders. It was bred for farm work such as cattle droving, sheep herding and cart pulling, and today serves as a guard dog, police dog and pet. It is a large, rugged dog standing about 59 to 68 cm.

faq.q: Do Bouviers des Flandres shed?
faq.a: They are sometimes called non-shedding but do lose hair; much of it is caught in the double coat, so weekly brushing is needed.

faq.q: Are Bouviers good with children?
faq.a: They are described as able to coexist well with children, though early socialization is recommended.

faq.q: Is the Bouvier des Flandres recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 191 in Group 1, Sheepdogs and Cattle Dogs.

cats/maine-coon.description: The Maine Coon is a large long-haired cat breed from Maine, USA, with a dense water-resistant coat, tufted ears and a bushy tail, known as the gentle giant.
cats/maine-coon.answer: The Maine Coon is a large domestic cat breed from the US state of Maine, where it is the official state cat. It is bred from one of North America's oldest landraces and is known for its long, dense coat. Weighing roughly 4.5 to 11 kg, it is commonly called the gentle giant and is often said to be dog-like.

faq.q: How big does a Maine Coon get?
faq.a: Weight is listed at about 4.5 to 11 kg, with males larger than females, and the body can reach up to 97 cm long including the tail.

faq.q: How long do Maine Coons live?
faq.a: Swedish insurance data put the median lifespan above 12.5 years, though a UK study found 9.71 years.

faq.q: Is the Maine Coon part raccoon?
faq.a: No. That is a myth; genetic studies show it descends from European cats brought to New England by settlers.

cats/ragdoll.description: The Ragdoll is a large American cat breed with a semi-long, silky colourpoint coat and blue eyes, known for a docile, placid and affectionate temperament.
cats/ragdoll.answer: The Ragdoll is a large cat breed developed in California in the 1960s by breeder Ann Baker. It has a semi-long, silky colourpoint coat and large blue eyes. Its name comes from its tendency to go limp and relaxed when picked up, and it is best known for a docile, affectionate nature.

faq.q: How big do Ragdoll cats get?
faq.a: Females weigh about 3.6 to 6.8 kg and males about 5.4 to 9.1 kg or more; full size can take up to four years.

faq.q: Do Ragdolls shed?
faq.a: They lack a dense undercoat, which the CFA says reduces shedding and matting, but shedding may increase in spring.

faq.q: How long do Ragdoll cats live?
faq.a: A 2025 UK study found a median age at death of 12.85 years.

cats/siamese.description: The Siamese is a slender cat breed from Thailand with a short, glossy colourpoint coat, blue almond-shaped eyes and a social, affectionate, outgoing nature.
cats/siamese.answer: The Siamese is one of the first distinctly recognised cat breeds, developed from the Wichianmat landrace of Thailand, once called Siam. It has a short, glossy colourpoint coat, blue almond-shaped eyes and a long, slender body. It is commonly described as affectionate, intelligent and very social.

faq.q: Why do Siamese cats have dark points?
faq.a: Their colourpoint pattern comes from a heat-sensitive enzyme that produces pigment only in cooler parts of the body, such as the ears, face, paws and tail.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Siamese and a Thai cat?
faq.a: Both descend from the Wichianmat, but the Thai keeps the traditional rounder build, while the modern Siamese is bred slender and angular.

faq.q: How long do Siamese cats live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 11.69 years, close to the average for all cats.

cats/bengal.description: The Bengal is a medium-to-large American hybrid cat breed bred from the Asian leopard cat and domestic cats, with a spotted, rosetted or marbled tabby coat.
cats/bengal.answer: The Bengal is a hybrid cat breed created by crossing the Asian leopard cat with domestic cats, notably the Egyptian Mau. It is known for a wild-looking tabby coat with spots, rosettes or marbling. It is a medium-to-large cat weighing roughly 3.5 to 9 kg, and its ownership is regulated in some places because of its wild ancestry.

faq.q: Are Bengal cats hypoallergenic?
faq.a: This is often claimed but has not been scientifically proven, and experts note that no cat is truly hypoallergenic.

faq.q: Is it legal to own a Bengal cat?
faq.a: In many places yes, but some countries, US states and cities restrict or ban them, particularly early generations close to the leopard cat.

faq.q: How big do Bengal cats get?
faq.a: They are a medium-to-large breed, weighing roughly 3.5 to 9 kg.

cats/british-shorthair.description: The British Shorthair is a sturdy, medium-to-large cat from Britain with a dense, plush coat, a broad round face and a calm temperament; the blue is best known.
cats/british-shorthair.answer: The British Shorthair is the pedigree form of Britain's native domestic cat, with a stocky body, thick coat and broad face. Its best-known colour is the British Blue, with a grey-blue coat and copper eyes. It typically weighs about 4 to 7 kg and is known for a relatively calm temperament.

faq.q: How big does a British Shorthair get?
faq.a: It typically weighs about 4 to 7 kg, with males noticeably larger than females.

faq.q: What colours do British Shorthairs come in?
faq.a: Blue is the best known, but the breed comes in many colours, including white, black, red and cream, in solid, tabby, colourpoint and bicolour patterns.

faq.q: How long do British Shorthairs live?
faq.a: Studies vary: a UK study found 9.58 years, while Swedish insurance data put the median above 12.5 years.

cats/sphynx.description: The Sphynx is a hairless cat breed from Canada with chamois-textured skin, large ears and lemon-shaped eyes, known as energetic, affectionate and dog-like.
cats/sphynx.answer: The Sphynx, also called the Canadian Sphynx, is a cat breed known for its lack of fur, developed from natural hairless mutations from the 1960s onward. Its skin feels like chamois leather and shows the colours and markings a coat would have. It is commonly described as extroverted, energetic and very affectionate.

faq.q: Are Sphynx cats hypoallergenic?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Cat allergies are triggered by a protein found in saliva and skin glands, not hair, so allergic people may still react.

faq.q: Are Sphynx cats completely hairless?
faq.a: Some are, but many have fine down on the skin, and some have hair on the nose, tail or toes.

faq.q: Do Sphynx cats need baths?
faq.a: Their skin produces greasy secretions and they make extra earwax, so regular cleaning of the skin, ears, nails and skin folds is needed.

cats/persian.description: The Persian is a long-haired cat breed associated with Iran, with a round face, short cobby body and a very long thick coat, described as quiet and placid.
cats/persian.answer: The Persian, or Persian Longhair, is a long-haired cat breed descended from cats exported from Iran and Afghanistan to Europe, and one of the most popular pedigree breeds. It has a round head, short cobby body and very long, thick coat, typically weighs about 3.5 to 7 kg, and is generally described as quiet and placid.

faq.q: How long do Persian cats live?
faq.a: Figures vary by study: a 2015 study in England found an average lifespan of 14.1 years, while a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 10.93 years.

faq.q: Do Persian cats need a lot of grooming?
faq.a: Yes. Their long, dense coat needs frequent brushing to prevent matting, and their eyes may need regular cleaning.

faq.q: What is a Traditional or doll-face Persian?
faq.a: It is the original Persian type with a more pronounced muzzle, as opposed to the flat-faced modern show type.

cats/siberian.description: The Siberian is a medium to large long-haired cat breed from Russia, powerfully built with a dense water-repellent triple coat and a playful, friendly nature.
cats/siberian.answer: The Siberian, formally the Siberian Forest Cat, is a centuries-old Russian landrace developed into a formal breed from the late 1980s and recognized by all major registries since 2006. It is a strong, medium to large cat of about 4.5 to 9 kg with a dense semi-long to long coat, commonly described as playful, friendly and easygoing.

faq.q: Are Siberian cats hypoallergenic?
faq.a: No cat is allergen-free. Studies found all Siberians tested produce some Fel d 1, though about half had lower levels than other breeds, so individual cats vary.

faq.q: How big does a Siberian cat get?
faq.a: Adults weigh on average 4.5 to 9 kg, with females considerably smaller than males, and they reach full size at about five years.

faq.q: Do Siberian cats shed?
faq.a: Yes. They molt heavily in spring and lightly in late summer, shed year-round and need grooming several times a week.

cats/bombay.description: The Bombay is a short-haired cat breed from the United States, a medium-sized muscular cat with a glossy jet-black coat, copper-gold eyes and a social nature.
cats/bombay.answer: The Bombay is a short-haired domestic cat breed developed in the United States from the late 1950s to resemble a miniature black panther. It is a medium-sized, muscular cat of about 2.5 to 5 kg with a sleek solid black coat and copper-golden eyes, and is described as highly social.

faq.q: How long do Bombay cats live?
faq.a: Healthy Bombays are reported to live about 15 years on average, and some have reached 20.

faq.q: Are Bombay cats good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as social, family-attached and attention-seeking, which is why they are often called suitable for children; individuals vary.

faq.q: How big does a Bombay cat get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized cat weighing about 2.5 to 5 kg, with males usually heavier than females.

cats/abyssinian.description: The Abyssinian is an old cat breed developed in Britain, named for Abyssinia: lithe and medium to large, with a short ticked coat and an active, social nature.
cats/abyssinian.answer: The Abyssinian, or Aby, is one of the oldest established cat breeds, developed in the United Kingdom and named after Abyssinia (Ethiopia), though genetic studies point to Southeast Asian and European roots. It is a lithe, muscular, medium to large cat with a short ticked coat and large ears, usually described as social, active and playful.

faq.q: Are Abyssinian cats lap cats?
faq.a: Generally not. They are commonly described as constantly exploring or playing, though very social and attached to their owners.

faq.q: Where do Abyssinian cats come from?
faq.a: The breed was developed in the United Kingdom and named after Abyssinia (Ethiopia), but genetic studies indicate cats from both Southeast Asia and Europe went into it.

faq.q: What is a ticked coat?
faq.a: In a ticked coat each hair has a light base and several darker bands of color, giving the Abyssinian its even, finely flecked look.

cats/russian-blue.description: The Russian Blue is a short-haired cat breed from Russia, small to moderate in size, with a dense silvery blue-grey double coat, green eyes and a quiet nature.
cats/russian-blue.answer: The Russian Blue is a pedigreed short-haired cat breed descended from a natural landrace thought to come from the port of Arkhangelsk in Russia. It is a small to moderate cat of about 3.6 to 6.8 kg with a plush, silver-tipped blue-grey double coat and green eyes, and is commonly described as quiet, intelligent and playful.

faq.q: How big does a Russian Blue get?
faq.a: Russian Blues are small to moderate cats, typically weighing about 3.6 to 6.8 kg when grown, with males usually larger than females.

faq.q: Are Russian Blues quiet?
faq.a: They are generally described as a quiet breed and reserved with strangers, though individuals vary.

faq.q: Is a Russian Blue the same as a British Blue?
faq.a: No. A British Blue is a blue British Shorthair, and the Chartreux and Korat are other separate blue breeds.

cats/norwegian-forest-cat.description: The Norwegian Forest Cat is a large long-haired cat breed from Norway, sturdy and long-legged, with a water-repellent double coat and a friendly nature.
cats/norwegian-forest-cat.answer: The Norwegian Forest Cat is a pedigreed domestic cat breed from Norway, adapted to a cold climate with a long, glossy, water-repellent coat over a woolly undercoat. It is larger than average and strongly built, and is described as friendly, intelligent and energetic.

faq.q: How big does a Norwegian Forest Cat get?
faq.a: It is larger than an average cat: females typically weigh about 3.6 to 8 kg and males about 4.5 to 9 kg.

faq.q: Are Norwegian Forest Cats good indoor cats?
faq.a: They are described as adapting to indoor life, though they are energetic climbers that appreciate space to climb and play.

faq.q: Is the Norwegian Forest Cat the same as the Maine Coon or Siberian?
faq.a: No. It is a separate breed from Norway, although longhaired cats like those ancestral to the Siberian may be among its ancestors.

cats/scottish-fold.description: The Scottish Fold is a medium to large cat breed from Scotland with forward-folded ears, a rounded look and a dominant gene for a cartilage and bone disorder.
cats/scottish-fold.answer: The Scottish Fold is a domestic cat breed from Scotland whose ears fold forward and down, giving an owl-like look. The fold comes from a dominant mutation that also causes feline osteochondrodysplasia, a cartilage and bone disorder affecting all folded cats, and the breed is banned from breeding in several countries and not recognized by some major registries.

faq.q: Why are Scottish Folds controversial?
faq.a: The mutation that folds the ears also causes osteochondrodysplasia, a cartilage and bone disorder that can lead to painful joint disease, so breeding is banned in several countries.

faq.q: Is the Scottish Fold recognized by all registries?
faq.a: No. The CFA recognizes it, but the GCCF and FIFe do not, because of its health problems.

faq.q: How big does a Scottish Fold get?
faq.a: It is a medium to large cat; males typically weigh 4 to 6 kg and females 2.7 to 4 kg.

cats/munchkin.description: The Munchkin is a US cat breed with very short legs caused by a dominant mutation; small to medium-sized, it is recognized by only some registries.
cats/munchkin.answer: The Munchkin is a domestic cat breed from the United States defined by very short legs, the result of a dominant chondrodysplasia mutation. It is a small to medium-sized cat of moderate build, and it is recognized by TICA and some other registries while others, including FIFe, the GCCF and the CFA, refuse it on welfare grounds.

faq.q: Why do Munchkin cats have short legs?
faq.a: Their short legs are caused by an autosomal dominant chondrodysplasia mutation; kittens inheriting two copies are not viable.

faq.q: Is the Munchkin recognized by the FIFe or CFA?
faq.a: No. FIFe, the GCCF and the CFA do not recognize the Munchkin; TICA, the WCF and a few other registries do.

faq.q: Can Munchkin cats jump?
faq.a: Sources differ: some say the short legs do not affect running and leaping, while others say jumping is limited.

cats/manx.description: The Manx is a medium-sized cat breed from the Isle of Man, often tailless, with long hind legs, a round head and thick double coat; described as social.
cats/manx.answer: The Manx is a domestic cat breed from the Isle of Man whose dominant mutation shortens or removes the tail. It is a medium-sized, muscular cat with hind legs longer than the front, a rounded head and a thick double coat, and is traditionally described as social, tame, active and a skilled hunter.

faq.q: Are all Manx cats tailless?
faq.a: No. Tail length varies even within one litter, from no tail at all to a full-length tail.

faq.q: Does having no tail affect a Manx cat's balance?
faq.a: No. Balance is controlled mainly by the inner ear, and Manx cats are reported not to have balance problems.

faq.q: What is a Cymric cat?
faq.a: The Cymric is the long-haired form of the Manx. Some registries treat it as a separate breed; others, such as the CFA, treat it as a Manx variety.

cats/turkish-angora.description: The Turkish Angora is an old natural cat breed from Ankara, Turkey: slender and elegant, with a silky coat, plumed tail and a playful, people-focused nature.
cats/turkish-angora.answer: The Turkish Angora, or Ankara cat, is one of the ancient natural cat breeds, originating in the Ankara region of central Anatolia, Turkey. It is a slender, fine-boned cat weighing roughly 2.5 to 5 kg, with a silky coat and a plumed tail, and is described as playful and intelligent.

faq.q: How big does a Turkish Angora get?
faq.a: It is a slender, fine-boned cat; listed weights are roughly 2.5 to 5 kg.

faq.q: Are Turkish Angoras always white?
faq.a: No. White is the best-known color, but many colors and patterns are accepted; chocolate, lavender and colorpoint are not.

faq.q: Is the Turkish Angora the same as the Persian?
faq.a: Historically the names were sometimes used interchangeably, but the Angora has always differed in type, especially from the modern flat-faced show Persian.

cats/egyptian-mau.description: The Egyptian Mau is a rare cat breed from Egypt, small to medium-sized and muscular, with a naturally spotted tabby coat, light green eyes and great speed.
cats/egyptian-mau.answer: The Egyptian Mau is a rare, small to medium-sized cat breed associated with Egypt and one of the few naturally spotted domestic breeds. It is muscular, with longer hind legs, a spotted coat, a scarab-like forehead marking and light green eyes.

faq.q: Is the Egyptian Mau the fastest domestic cat?
faq.a: It is described as the fastest domestic cat breed, clocked at more than 48 km/h (30 mph), helped by its long hind legs and flank skin flap.

faq.q: Is the Egyptian Mau naturally spotted?
faq.a: Yes. It is one of the few naturally spotted tabby breeds of domestic cat.

faq.q: What colors does the Egyptian Mau come in?
faq.a: Accepted colors are silver spotted tabby, bronze spotted tabby and black smoke.

cats/devon-rex.description: The Devon Rex is a short-haired cat breed from Devon, England, with a medium build, large wide-set ears, big eyes and a soft, wavy curled coat.
cats/devon-rex.answer: The Devon Rex is a short-haired domestic cat breed that emerged in Devon, England, around 1960. It has a medium build, an elfin wedge-shaped head with very large ears and eyes, and a soft coat that curls into waves.

faq.q: Where does the Devon Rex come from?
faq.a: The breed began in Devon, England, from a curly-coated kitten found in Buckfastleigh in 1960.

faq.q: Is the Devon Rex the same as the Cornish Rex?
faq.a: No. Test breedings showed the Devon Rex curl is caused by a different mutation from the Cornish Rex, since crosses between the two produced straight-coated kittens.

faq.q: What does a Devon Rex coat look like?
faq.a: It is short, dense and soft, curling inward into waves or ripples, with crinkled whiskers and eyebrows; some areas such as the neck can be thinly furred.

cats/american-wirehair.description: The American Wirehair is a rare cat breed from upstate New York, a sturdy American Shorthair relative with a springy wiry coat and a gentle, even temperament.
cats/american-wirehair.answer: The American Wirehair is a domestic cat breed from upstate New York, United States, defined by a wiry coat caused by a dominant mutation. It is a moderate, sturdy cat much like the American Shorthair, usually described as gentle, quiet and playful.

faq.q: Is the American Wirehair rare?
faq.a: Yes. As of 2017 it was ranked the rarest of the 41 breeds recognized by the Cat Fanciers' Association.

faq.q: Does an American Wirehair need much grooming?
faq.a: The wiry coat is reported to need little grooming, although lighter-colored cats may need protection from the sun.

faq.q: Is the wirehair coat gene dominant?
faq.a: Yes. The wirehair trait is dominant, so a cross between a Wirehair and another cat can produce wire-coated kittens.

cats/turkish-van.description: The Turkish Van is a rare, large semi-long-haired cat breed from Turkey, developed in the UK, white with color on head and tail, and energetic and intelligent.
cats/turkish-van.answer: The Turkish Van is a rare, semi-long-haired cat breed developed in the United Kingdom in the 1950s from cats obtained in Turkey. It is one of the larger breeds, with males weighing about 5 to 9 kg, and it is defined by the Van pattern: a white cat with color mainly on the head and tail.

faq.q: How big does a Turkish Van get?
faq.a: It is one of the larger breeds: males weigh about 5 to 9 kg and females about 3 to 5 kg, and full maturity takes three to five years.

faq.q: Do Turkish Vans like water?
faq.a: The breed is often said to be fascinated by water, though some pet writers think it likes water no more than other cats.

faq.q: Are Turkish Vans lap cats?
faq.a: They are described as affectionate and keen to be near their owners, but not usually lap cats, and many dislike being picked up.

cats/oriental-shorthair.description: The Oriental Shorthair is a cat breed developed in the US and UK from the Siamese: medium-sized, slender and muscular, in many colors, and social and vocal.
cats/oriental-shorthair.answer: The Oriental Shorthair is a domestic cat breed developed from, and closely related to, the Siamese, keeping its slender body and wedge-shaped head but in a wide range of colors and patterns. It is a medium-sized cat, usually green-eyed, commonly described as social, curious and talkative.

faq.q: What is the difference between an Oriental Shorthair and a Siamese?
faq.a: The Oriental keeps the modern Siamese body and head but comes in a wide range of colors and patterns instead of only points, and is usually green-eyed rather than blue-eyed.

faq.q: Are Oriental Shorthairs vocal?
faq.a: Yes. Like the Siamese, they are commonly described as natural conversationalists, and many are quite vocal.

faq.q: How big does an Oriental Shorthair get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized cat; males average about 3.5 to 5.5 kg and females under 3.5 kg.

cats/chartreux.description: The Chartreux is a rare cat breed from France, muscular and cobby with a dense blue-grey water-resistant coat, copper eyes and a quiet, affectionate nature.
cats/chartreux.answer: The Chartreux is a rare domestic cat breed from France, known for its blue-grey double coat and orange or copper eyes. It is large and muscular on fairly short legs, and is usually described as quiet, observant and affectionate.

faq.q: Are Chartreux cats quiet?
faq.a: Yes. They are commonly described as rarely meowing, and some are almost completely mute.

faq.q: What color is a Chartreux?
faq.a: The Chartreux is known for a blue (silver-grey) coat, dense and water-resistant, with a dense water-resistant coat and orange or copper eyes.

faq.q: Are Chartreux good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as non-aggressive, affectionate and good with children and other animals, though individuals vary.

cats/burmese.description: The Burmese is a cat breed originating in Burma and developed in the US and UK: small to medium, muscular, with a short glossy coat and a social, vocal nature.
cats/burmese.answer: The Burmese is a pedigreed cat breed originating in Burma and developed through selective breeding in the United States and Britain, which now have different standards. It is a small to medium but substantial cat of about 4 to 6 kg with a short satin-like coat, known for being social, playful and vocal.

faq.q: How long do Burmese cats live?
faq.a: One UK study of veterinary records found an average life expectancy of 14.42 years in a sample of 45 Burmese.

faq.q: What is the difference between American and European Burmese?
faq.a: The European type is slimmer with a wedge-shaped head, while the American type is stockier with a broader head, round eyes and a shorter muzzle.

faq.q: Are Burmese cats vocal?
faq.a: Yes. They are described as persistently vocal, though their voices are softer than those of the Siamese.

cats/birman.description: The Birman, or Sacred Cat of Burma, is a medium-sized long-haired colorpoint cat breed developed in France, with deep blue eyes and white-gloved paws.
cats/birman.answer: The Birman, also called the Sacred Cat of Burma, is a long-haired colorpoint domestic cat first recognized in France in 1925. It is a medium-sized cat with a silky, single coat, deep sapphire-blue eyes and symmetrical white gloves on all four paws.

faq.q: How long do Birman cats live?
faq.a: One UK study of veterinary records found an average life expectancy of 14.39 years in a sample of 38 Birmans.

faq.q: Do Birmans mat easily?
faq.a: Their medium-long silky coat has no undercoat, so it is much less prone to matting than a Persian or Himalayan coat.

faq.q: Why do Birmans have white paws?
faq.a: Symmetrical pure white gloves on each paw are the breed's trademark and are required by the breed standard.

cats/himalayan.description: The Himalayan is a long-haired cat from Persian and Siamese crosses, developed in the US and UK: cobby and medium to large, with color points and blue eyes.
cats/himalayan.answer: The Himalayan, or Colorpoint Persian, is a long-haired cat of Persian type with blue eyes and Siamese-style point coloring, developed by crossing Persians with Siamese. It is a medium to large, cobby cat with a round, flat face and a long, thick coat; several registries treat it as a Persian color variant.

faq.q: Is a Himalayan cat a Persian?
faq.a: The CFA and GCCF treat the Himalayan as a color variant of the Persian, while some other registries, such as the ACFA, list it as a separate breed.

faq.q: Why do Himalayans have blue eyes?
faq.a: Their blue eyes and point coloring come from the Siamese cats used in the original Persian crosses.

faq.q: Do Himalayan cats have health problems?
faq.a: As a flat-faced breed, the Himalayan is reported to be prone to breathing and eye problems, and polycystic kidney disease is also reported in the breed.

cats/japanese-bobtail.description: The Japanese Bobtail is a cat breed from Japan, medium-sized and lean, with a short kinked bobtail, a soft silky coat and an active, talkative nature.
cats/japanese-bobtail.answer: The Japanese Bobtail is a domestic cat breed from Japan with a short, kinked tail that resembles a rabbit's. It is a medium-sized, lean and muscular cat of about 2.7 to 4 kg, known for centuries in Japanese folklore and art, and commonly described as active, intelligent and talkative.

faq.q: How long do Japanese Bobtails live?
faq.a: The breed's average lifespan is given as 9 to 15 years.

faq.q: Does the bobtail cause health problems?
faq.a: The bobtail gene is not associated with spinal or bone abnormalities, unlike the gene behind the Manx cat's tail.

faq.q: Do Japanese Bobtails shed?
faq.a: They are reported to have minimal to medium shedding, and the coat is easy to groom.

cats/snowshoe.description: The Snowshoe is a rare cat breed from the United States, a medium-sized short-haired pointed cat with blue eyes, white feet and an affectionate, social nature.
cats/snowshoe.answer: The Snowshoe is a rare short-haired cat breed that originated in Philadelphia, United States, in the 1960s from Siamese and bicolor American Shorthair crosses. It is a medium-sized, athletic pointed cat with blue eyes and white feet, commonly described as affectionate and social.

faq.q: Why is the Snowshoe cat rare?
faq.a: The breed's markings rely on genes that are hard to control, so few kittens match the standard's white feet and facial pattern.

faq.q: Are Snowshoe cats good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as social and compatible with children and other pets, though individuals vary.

faq.q: Do Snowshoe cats need much grooming?
faq.a: Their short, smooth coat with no noticeable undercoat is reported to need little grooming.

cats/exotic-shorthair.description: The Exotic Shorthair is an American cat breed developed as a short-haired Persian: medium to large, round-faced, with a short, dense coat in all colors.
cats/exotic-shorthair.answer: The Exotic Shorthair is a cat breed developed in the United States as a short-haired version of the Persian. It shares the Persian's medium to large, rounded build and flat-faced look, but has a short, dense coat instead of long hair.

faq.q: What is the difference between an Exotic Shorthair and a Persian?
faq.a: The Exotic is essentially a Persian with a short, dense coat. Body shape, head and face are very similar; the main difference is coat length.
