faq.q: Can Exotic Shorthairs have long hair?
faq.a: Yes. Some carry the recessive longhair gene from Persian outcrosses, and two carriers can produce longhaired kittens, which registries classify in different ways.

faq.q: What health problems do Exotic Shorthairs have?
faq.a: Conditions reported in the breed include brachycephalic airway problems, corneal sequestrum, dystocia and polycystic kidney disease, for which DNA screening of breeding cats is recommended.

cats/european-shorthair.description: The European Shorthair is a Scandinavian pedigree cat that resembles Europe's common house cat: medium-sized, muscular, with a short, dense, glossy coat.
cats/european-shorthair.answer: The European Shorthair is a pedigreed cat breed, developed mainly in Scandinavia, that is meant to resemble the typical domestic cat of Europe. It is a medium-sized, muscular cat with a short, glossy coat, generally described as active and friendly.

faq.q: Is the European Shorthair the same as a British Shorthair?
faq.a: No. They were once judged as one breed, but FIFe separated the Scandinavian type in 1982; the British Shorthair is cobbier, with a shorter muzzle and thicker coat.

faq.q: Are European Shorthairs friendly?
faq.a: They are commonly described as friendly toward people of all ages, good with other cats and tolerant of dogs, though individuals vary.

faq.q: Where is the European Shorthair popular?
faq.a: Mostly in Scandinavia and Germany. It is the national cat of Finland and is listed as an endangered breed in Sweden.

cats/dragon-li.description: The Dragon Li, or Chinese Li Hua, is a cat breed from China: a sturdy, shorthaired cat with a black mackerel tabby coat and a gentle temperament.
cats/dragon-li.answer: The Dragon Li, also called the Chinese Li Hua, is a recently established breed developed in China in the early 2000s from the country's native li hua mao landrace. It is a sturdy, cobby shorthaired cat that comes only as a black mackerel tabby and is described as gentle and a capable hunter.

faq.q: Is the Dragon Li a recognized breed?
faq.a: Only by China's Cat Aficionado Association. The CFA accepted it in 2010 but removed it in 2015, so no major international registry recognizes it.

faq.q: What colors does the Dragon Li come in?
faq.a: Only black mackerel tabby on a brown-yellow ground. Any other color or pattern is not allowed by the standard.

faq.q: Why is it called Dragon Li?
faq.a: It is named after the li hua mao landrace, with 'Dragon' added for the dragon's symbolism of power and good luck in Chinese folklore.

cats/ragamuffin.description: The Ragamuffin is an American cat breed split from the Ragdoll in 1994: a large, heavy-boned cat with a soft, thick coat in any color, known for being friendly.
cats/ragamuffin.answer: The Ragamuffin is a domestic cat breed from the United States that was once considered a variant of the Ragdoll and became a separate breed in 1994. It is a substantial, heavy-boned cat with a thick, silky coat in any color and pattern, and is known for its friendly personality.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Ragamuffin and a Ragdoll?
faq.a: Ragdolls must have pointed coloring, while Ragamuffins are allowed any color and pattern. Ragamuffins also have rounder walnut-shaped eyes, rounded head contours and a flatter topline.

faq.q: Are Ragamuffins friendly?
faq.a: Yes, the breed is commonly described as friendly, and temperament was a focus of its development, though individuals vary.

faq.q: When did the Ragamuffin become a breed?
faq.a: It was established as a separate breed in 1994, when a group of breeders left the IRCA Ragdoll registry.

cats/balinese.description: The Balinese is a long-haired Siamese-type cat with Thai roots: slender, with a silky medium coat, pointed coloring, blue eyes and a sociable, vocal nature.
cats/balinese.answer: The Balinese is a long-haired cat breed that arose as a natural mutation of the Siamese, whose ancestors came from Thailand, and was developed as a breed in the United States from the 1950s. It is a slender, graceful cat with a silky medium-length coat, Siamese-style points and blue eyes, and is described as sociable, vocal and playful.

faq.q: Is a Balinese cat just a long-haired Siamese?
faq.a: Essentially yes. It originated as a natural long-hair mutation of the Siamese and is the same type of cat with a medium-length silky coat and a plumed tail.

faq.q: Do Balinese cats meow a lot?
faq.a: They are commonly described as vocal and persistent talkers, though usually at a lower volume than the Siamese.

faq.q: Is the Balinese from Bali?
faq.a: No. The name refers to the grace of Balinese dancers; the breed descends from Siamese cats from Thailand and was developed in the United States.

cats/tonkinese.description: The Tonkinese is a cat breed recognized first in Canada, bred from Siamese and Burmese: medium-sized, muscular, with a pointed or mink coat and a lively nature.
cats/tonkinese.answer: The Tonkinese is a domestic cat breed produced by crossing the Siamese and the Burmese, first recognized as a distinct breed in Canada in 1965. It is a medium-sized, surprisingly muscular cat with a pointed, mink or sepia coat, and is described as active, vocal and people-oriented.

faq.q: What is a mink Tonkinese?
faq.a: Mink is the breed's signature intermediate pattern, with a light body harmonizing with the point color and aquamarine eyes. It results from one Siamese and one Burmese pattern gene.

faq.q: Are Tonkinese cats vocal?
faq.a: They are described as vocal, but with a softer, sweeter voice than the Siamese, similar to the Burmese.

faq.q: Do Tonkinese cats like to be alone?
faq.a: They are commonly described as people-oriented and can become lonesome or bored without company and activity.

cats/cornish-rex.description: The Cornish Rex is a British cat breed from Cornwall: slender and muscular, with a fine, curly coat made only of down hair, large ears and a galloping run.
cats/cornish-rex.answer: The Cornish Rex is a domestic cat breed that originated in Cornwall, Great Britain, in the 1950s. It is a slender, muscular cat whose fine, curly coat consists only of down hair, and it is sometimes called the Greyhound of cats for its sleek look and galloping run.

faq.q: Are Cornish Rex cats hypoallergenic?
faq.a: No. Cat allergies come from the Fel d 1 protein in saliva and dander, not from hair, so a Cornish Rex can still trigger reactions, though some people report milder ones.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Cornish Rex and a Devon Rex?
faq.a: They are caused by different mutations. The Devon Rex has shortened guard hairs and sheds, while the Cornish Rex has no guard hairs, only curly down.

faq.q: Do Cornish Rex cats get cold?
faq.a: Yes, their thin coat makes them sensitive to low temperatures, so they are best kept indoors in warm, dry conditions.

cats/minuet.description: The Minuet, formerly the Napoleon, is an American Persian and Munchkin cross: short-legged, flat-faced, long or short coat, recognized by TICA but few others.
cats/minuet.answer: The Minuet, originally called the Napoleon, is a hybrid cat breed developed in the United States from 1996 by crossing Persians with Munchkins. It combines the Munchkin's short legs with the Persian's shortened face and comes in long-haired and short-haired varieties; most major registries do not recognize it because of welfare concerns.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Minuet and a Napoleon cat?
faq.a: They are the same breed. TICA changed the name from Napoleon to Minuet in 2015, though some registries still use the original name.

faq.q: Why is the Minuet not recognized by most registries?
faq.a: Registries such as the CFA, FIFe, GCCF and WCF do not recognize it because of welfare concerns about health problems linked to dwarfism and a flat face.

faq.q: Do Minuet cats have health problems?
faq.a: Conditions reported in the breed include achondrodysplasia, osteoarthritis risk, spinal and chest deformities, and brachycephalic breathing, eye and dental problems.

cats/korat.description: The Korat is an ancient Thai cat breed: small to medium and heavy for its size, with a silver-tipped blue coat, green eyes and a playful, vocal nature.
cats/korat.answer: The Korat is a natural cat breed from Thailand, named after Nakhon Ratchasima Province and traditionally known as a good-luck cat. It is a small to medium, semi-cobby cat that is heavy for its size, with a silver-tipped blue-grey coat, a heart-shaped head and large green eyes, and is described as intelligent, playful and vocal.

faq.q: Why is the Korat called a good-luck cat?
faq.a: In Thailand Korats were traditionally given in pairs to newlyweds or highly esteemed people to bring good luck, and were once given only as gifts.

faq.q: What color is a Korat cat?
faq.a: Korats come only in silver-tipped blue, a shimmering blue-grey coat, with green eyes in adults.

faq.q: How big does a Korat get?
faq.a: It is a small to medium cat that feels heavy for its size; reference data lists about 2 to 4.5 kg.

cats/ojos-azules.description: The Ojos Azules was a rare American cat breed from New Mexico: medium-sized and shorthaired, with deep blue eyes from a dominant gene. It is now extinct.
cats/ojos-azules.answer: The Ojos Azules, Spanish for 'Blue Eyes', was a rare shorthaired cat breed that originated in New Mexico, USA, in the 1980s. It was a medium-sized cat whose deep blue eyes came from a dominant mutation not linked to coat color, but breeding stopped because of lethal side effects and the breed is now considered extinct.

faq.q: Is the Ojos Azules cat extinct?
faq.a: Yes. Breeders stopped working with the blue-eye mutation because of lethal side effects, and the breed is officially considered extinct.

faq.q: What does Ojos Azules mean?
faq.a: It is Spanish for 'Blue Eyes', referring to the breed's deep blue eyes.

faq.q: Are there other blue-eyed breeds like the Ojos Azules?
faq.a: Other dominant blue-eye genes found in Kazakhstan and Russia are the basis of developing breeds such as the Altai, Topaz and Celestial, but these are not Ojos Azules.

cats/ocicat.description: The Ocicat is an American cat breed that looks wild but is all domestic: medium to large and athletic, with a spotted tabby coat and a famously dog-like nature.
cats/ocicat.answer: The Ocicat is an all-domestic cat breed from the United States, created from Siamese and Abyssinian crosses with later American Shorthair input. It is a medium to large, athletic cat with a spotted tabby coat that resembles the ocelot, and its temperament is often described as dog-like.

faq.q: Does the Ocicat have wild cat DNA?
faq.a: No. Despite its wild look and ocelot-inspired name, it was created entirely from domestic breeds: Siamese, Abyssinian and American Shorthair.

faq.q: How big does an Ocicat get?
faq.a: It is a medium to large cat; adults weigh about 2.5 to 6.5 kg.

faq.q: Can Ocicats be trained?
faq.a: They are often described as dog-like, and many can reportedly be trained to fetch, walk on a leash and come when called.

cats/american-curl.description: The American Curl is a cat breed from California known for ears that curl backward: medium-sized, with a soft, silky long or short coat that is easy to keep.
cats/american-curl.answer: The American Curl is a cat breed from Lakewood, California, known for ears that curl back from the face due to a spontaneous mutation. It is a medium-sized cat with a soft, silky coat in longhaired and shorthaired versions.

faq.q: Are American Curl kittens born with curled ears?
faq.a: No. Kittens are born with straight ears, which begin to curl within 48 hours and set in their final shape at about four months.

faq.q: How big does an American Curl get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized cat; reference data lists about 3 to 5 kg, with females smaller than males.

faq.q: Does the American Curl have the same problems as the Scottish Fold?
faq.a: The curl mutation is different from the fold mutation, and a cat with two copies of the curl gene observed over two years showed no abnormalities.

cats/havana-brown.description: The Havana Brown is a British-founded cat breed: moderate and muscular, with a short, solid warm-brown coat, green eyes and a curious, people-focused nature.
cats/havana-brown.answer: The Havana Brown is a pedigreed cat breed created by British fanciers in the 1950s from chocolate-carrying Siamese and black domestic shorthairs. It is a moderately sized, muscular cat with a short, solid warm-brown coat and green eyes, and is described as intelligent, curious and very attached to its family.

faq.q: Why is it called a Havana Brown?
faq.a: The name most likely refers to its coat color, which resembles Havana cigars, though some link it to the Havana rabbit.

faq.q: Can Havana Browns be left alone?
faq.a: They are described as very attached to their families and do not thrive when left alone for long periods.

faq.q: Is the Havana Brown rare?
faq.a: Yes. The USA-type Havana Brown is considered endangered, with only 15 catteries registered worldwide as of 2024.

cats/pixie-bob.description: The Pixie-bob is an American cat breed bred to look like a bobcat: medium to large, often polydactyl, with a short tail, spotted tabby coat and sociable nature.
cats/pixie-bob.answer: The Pixie-bob is a pedigreed cat breed developed in the United States from the mid-1980s, originally claimed to have bobcat ancestry but generally regarded as wholly domestic. It is a medium to large, often polydactyl cat with a short tail and a black spotted tabby coat, and is described as intelligent, social and active.

faq.q: Is the Pixie-bob part bobcat?
faq.a: The breed was originally claimed to have bobcat ancestry, but reported DNA testing found no bobcat markers, and Pixie-bobs are treated as fully domestic.

faq.q: How big do Pixie-bobs get?
faq.a: On average they usually do not exceed about 5 kg, similar to a medium to large domestic cat, and they can keep growing for up to four years.

faq.q: Do Pixie-bobs meow?
faq.a: Most meow little if at all and instead communicate with chirps, chatters and growls.

cats/donskoy.description: The Donskoy, or Don Sphynx, is a hairless cat breed from Russia: medium-sized and muscular, with wrinkled skin, large ears and a very social, active nature.
cats/donskoy.answer: The Donskoy, also called the Don Sphynx or Russian Hairless, is a hairless cat breed that originated in Rostov-on-Don, Russia, in 1987. It is a medium-sized, muscular cat with wrinkled skin and large ears, and its hairlessness is caused by a dominant mutation unrelated to the Sphynx.

faq.q: Is the Donskoy the same as a Sphynx?
faq.a: No. The Sphynx's hairlessness comes from a recessive mutation, while the Donskoy's comes from a dominant one, and the breeds are not related.

faq.q: Do Donskoy cats need grooming?
faq.a: Yes. They need frequent grooming despite having no coat, though over-bathing can make their skin very oily.

faq.q: Are Donskoy cats good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as gentle, social and good with children, and they do best with company rather than long periods alone.

cats/peterbald.description: The Peterbald is a hairless cat breed from St. Petersburg, Russia: slim, muscular and Oriental in type, bald or lightly coated, affectionate and curious.
cats/peterbald.answer: The Peterbald is a hairless cat breed created in St. Petersburg, Russia, in 1994 by crossing a Donskoy with an Oriental Shorthair. It has a slim, elegant Oriental build and a dominant hair-losing gene, and is described as affectionate, curious and energetic.

faq.q: Are Peterbald cats always hairless?
faq.a: No. They can be born bald, flocked, velour, brush or straight-coated, and those with hair other than straight coats may lose it over time.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Peterbald and a Donskoy?
faq.a: The Peterbald was bred from the Donskoy and the Oriental Shorthair, so it carries the same dominant hairless gene but has a slimmer Oriental body type.

faq.q: Are Peterbalds affectionate?
faq.a: They are commonly described as sweet-tempered and affectionate, tending to follow their owners and get on with children and other pets.

cats/aegean.description: The Aegean cat is a natural landrace from Greece's Cycladic Islands: medium-sized, muscular and semi-longhaired, usually bicolor with white, lively and social.
cats/aegean.answer: The Aegean is a naturally occurring landrace of domestic cat from the Cycladic Islands of Greece and western Turkey, considered the only native Greek cat variety. It is a medium-sized, muscular, semi-longhaired cat, usually bicolor or tricolor with white, and is described as intelligent, active and communicative.

faq.q: Is the Aegean cat a recognized breed?
faq.a: Not yet. Greek breeders began formal breeding in the early 1990s, but no major cat registry has recognized it.

faq.q: Do Aegean cats like water?
faq.a: Yes, they are noted for an affinity for water and fishing, fitting their life around island fishing ports.

faq.q: Can an Aegean cat live in an apartment?
faq.a: It is described as a social pet that tolerates apartment living rather well.

cats/cymric.description: The Cymric is a Canadian cat breed, the semi-longhaired form of the Manx: medium to large, compact and muscular, often tailless, with a dense double coat.
cats/cymric.answer: The Cymric is a cat breed developed in Canada in the 1960s as a semi-longhaired form of the Manx, whose bloodline comes from the Isle of Man; some registries treat it as a longhaired Manx. It is a compact, muscular, medium to large cat with a dense double coat and, in many cats, no tail.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Cymric and a Manx?
faq.a: Apart from the Cymric's semi-long coat they are the same, and both types can appear in one litter. Some registries treat the Cymric as a longhaired Manx.

faq.q: Do all Cymric cats have no tail?
faq.a: No. Tails range from completely absent (rumpy) to short stumps and near-full length, and fully tailed cats are kept as breeding stock.

faq.q: Is the Cymric from Wales?
faq.a: No. The name comes from Cymru, the Welsh name for Wales, but the breed was developed in Canada from Manx cats of the Isle of Man.
